tree-house-cafe-boulder-creek.title: The Tree House Cafe: The Boulder Creek Coffee Shop With Redwoods Inside It
tree-house-cafe-boulder-creek.html:
There are real redwoods growing up through the middle of the Tree House Cafe. These aren't painted redwoods or decorations. Living trunks pass through the building, and the seating is arranged around them. The trees gave the cafe its name. They're also why people who drive Highway 9 once a year remember stopping there.

The Tree House sits at 13266 Highway 9, at the north end of the Boulder Creek business district. It's close enough to the creek that the air changes when you step out of the car. Visit Santa Cruz County describes it as a place where "nostalgic Giant Redwoods grace the interior of this uniquely progressive cafe/espresso bar." That covers the essentials.

What it is

The Tree House is a coffee shop first. It has an espresso bar, drip coffee, and the expected range of drinks, plus breakfast and a lunch counter with sandwiches, bagels, and baked goods. Service is at the counter rather than at the table. It's the larger of the town's two coffee shops, with room to sit, work, and socialize, and the person making your drink is likely to recognize you the second time.

Boulder Creek has several options for coffee and breakfast, but they're not interchangeable. Jenna Sue's is the coffeehouse downtown in the middle of the shops. Bella's is a sit-down diner. The Tree House is where you go for the trees, a quiet table, and a slower half hour before the day gets moving.

Locals also use it as a working spot. You'll see laptops, notebooks, paperbacks, and people taking their time over a long coffee.

For me it's the quick-stop spot: a latte in hand when I'm across the way at the fire station, or a scoop of ice cream on a hot day, creekside. Some businesses are destinations; this one is a habit, and I mean that as high praise.

Built around the trees

Most cafes add their setting through decoration. The Tree House was built around what was already standing. The redwoods rise through the floor and continue through the roof. The interior fits around the trees.

That changes how the room sounds and how the light falls. It also makes the seating a little irregular, with tables tucked into spaces that wouldn't exist in a rectangular room. The arrangement follows the trunks rather than forcing the trees into a conventional floor plan.

For someone visiting the valley, the cafe offers a photograph that helps explain why people choose to live here. For someone who lives here, it's simply a place to stop on a Tuesday.

Hours

Open at 6 a.m. Monday through Friday and 7 a.m. on weekends, closing at 2:30 p.m. every day. That's the same schedule Jenna Sue's keeps downtown, so the town's two coffee shops share the earliest doors in Boulder Creek.

The menu

The boards change and prices move, so treat this as the shape of it and let the counter be current.

  • Breakfast: breakfast sandwiches on a bagel, croissant, or English muffin, breakfast and veggie burritos, avocado toast on sourdough, a lox bagel with capers, biscuits and gravy, steel cut oats, a yogurt parfait, fruit and cottage cheese, and bagels with house-made cream cheeses in pesto, jalapeno, and sundried tomato.
  • Lunch: a build-your-own sandwich counter with four breads, six meats, and four cheeses, plus the named house sandwiches: the Noel (ham or turkey with bacon), the Ernest (an Italian stack on a French roll), the Bob (tuna with oil and vinegar), and the Sunflower (avocado and provolone on seeded bread). Wraps, a classic BLT, grilled cheese, PB and J, and a soup of the day round it out.
  • Salads: Caesar, Cobb, spinach, and the Tree House salad, a tuna-stuffed avocado on romaine.
  • Drinks and sweets: the full espresso range, teas, Italian sodas, Tree House chillers and frozen lemonade in season, and Marianne's ice cream by the scoop.

Finding it between visits

The Tree House doesn't keep a website. It uses social media, as many small businesses in this valley do. Current information appears on its Facebook page and Instagram rather than on a permanent website.

The phone number is 831-610-8912, and someone is likely to pick up.

Menu items and specials change, especially at the shoulder of the seasons. Check the cafe's own Facebook or Instagram, or call, before you drive up for something specific.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are the redwoods really inside the building?

Yes. Living redwoods pass through the interior of the cafe. That's where the name comes from.

Does the Tree House Cafe have a website?

No. It posts on Facebook and Instagram instead. For anything time-sensitive, call 831-610-8912.

What does it serve?

Coffee and espresso drinks, breakfast, and a lunch counter with sandwiches, bagels, and baked goods. It's counter service rather than table service.

Where is it exactly?

13266 Highway 9, at the north end of the Boulder Creek business district, near the creek. It's a short distance up from the main downtown block.

Is it the same as the Tree House in Australia?

No. This can cause confusion online. There's an unrelated business with a near-identical name in Boulder Creek, Queensland. If a page you find is in Australia, it's not this cafe.

Last reviewed August 12, 2026. The cafe has no website, so hours and menu items live on its own social channels, which are the current source.

For the rest of the town's coffee and kitchens, see where to eat in Boulder Creek and the food and drink listings. Browse the business directory or the rest of our Around Town guides. Spot something out of date? Tell us.

san-lorenzo-valley-schools-guide.title: San Lorenzo Valley Schools: How the District Works
san-lorenzo-valley-schools-guide.html:
The short version

  • One valley, one district. San Lorenzo Valley Unified runs five schools from its offices at 325 Marion Avenue in Ben Lomond. Nearly every public school student from Boulder Creek to Felton passes through them.
  • The campuses: Boulder Creek Elementary is in town. SLV Elementary is in Felton. SLV Middle and SLV High sit side by side on the Felton campus off Highway 9.
  • The charter is a separate application. SLV Charter School runs homeschool hybrids, Nature Academy, and Coast Redwood High School out of Ben Lomond, with its own enrollment.
  • Enrollment starts with a phone call to your school's registrar, not an online form. Transfers between valley elementary schools require separate paperwork.
  • Busing exists but is limited and paid. One route serves Boulder Creek Elementary. K-12 students ride METRO free.

Every school-day morning in the valley runs downhill. Boulder Creek families head south on Highway 9, past Brookdale and Ben Lomond. By 8 a.m., the Felton campus has absorbed most of the valley's middle and high school students. That single road shapes the district. There's one of nearly everything, most trips require a drive, and the people at the school office tend to know your child's name by October.

Here is how San Lorenzo Valley Unified is organized, what each campus is for, and where to find a date, bus, or transfer form. For the 2026-27 calendar in detail, including every back-to-school night, see our back-to-school guide. For preschool, daycare, and the licensed-care landscape, see schools, preschools, and daycare in the valley.

One district, seven communities

SLVUSD covers Boulder Creek, Brookdale, Ben Lomond, Felton, Lompico, Zayante, and Mount Hermon. The district office is at 325 Marion Avenue in Ben Lomond and can be reached at 831-336-5194.

The geography matters more than the organizational chart. The district stretches along twenty miles of two-lane highway. That leads to fewer campuses, longer rides, and one high school that nearly every family has an opinion about. It works differently from a flatland district with four elementary schools inside a two-mile square.

One clarification helps when searching online. Our district is San Lorenzo Valley Unified, at slvusd.org. It's routinely confused with San Lorenzo Unified in the East Bay, a separate district with a similar name and a similar-looking website.

The campuses

Boulder Creek Elementary, 400 Lomond Street, 831-338-6413. This is the in-town campus, a short walk from downtown, and the only SLVUSD school inside Boulder Creek. Its website has registration information, the bell schedule, a drop-off and pick-up map worth reading before your first morning, and information about the Parent Club. News and announcements appear on the school's own page.

San Lorenzo Valley Elementary, in Felton. This is the valley's other elementary school, at sle.slvusd.org. Attendance areas determine which elementary school a child attends. Moving between the two requires an intradistrict transfer, not a phone call.

San Lorenzo Valley Middle School, ms.slvusd.org, serves grades six through eight on the Felton campus.

San Lorenzo Valley High School, 7105 Highway 9 in Felton, 831-335-4425. More details appear below.

San Lorenzo Valley Charter School, 325 Marion Avenue in Ben Lomond, charter.slvusd.org. The charter includes several separate programs.

The charter programs, which are not one thing

The district's alternative programs sit under the charter, with distinct options for nearly every stage:

  • Heartwood Homeschool (TK to first grade) and Quail Hollow Homeschool (grades two to five), two-day hybrids meeting Tuesdays and Thursdays.
  • Coast Redwood Middle School (grades six to eight), a two-day hybrid with a project-based emphasis, and Quail Hollow Integrated Arts, a three-day hybrid pairing online coursework with classroom time.
  • Nature Academy (grades six to eight), a traditional five-day program.
  • Coast Redwood High School (grades nine to twelve), a hybrid independent study high school accredited by WASC, with classroom hours Monday through Thursday and Friday conferences.

These programs offer alternatives to a five-day comprehensive campus. Charter enrollment requires a separate application from district enrollment. The charter programs page carries the current list.

San Lorenzo Valley High School

The Cougars' campus is at 7105 Highway 9 in Felton. It's the valley's only comprehensive high school.

SLV High offers Advanced Placement courses, Career and Technical Education pathways, dual enrollment with Cabrillo College, a Running Start program, and alternative education. Its Performing Arts Center supports music and theatre programs with help from boosters. Academic counseling, a College and Career Center, and mental health support operate through the counseling office. Start at hs.slvusd.org and use the school's own pages for information tied to a specific date.

Athletics. SLV fields roughly twenty sports across three seasons. Fall includes football, cross country, girls golf, girls tennis, girls volleyball, boys and girls water polo, and girls flag football. Winter includes basketball, soccer, and wrestling. Spring includes baseball, softball, track and field, swimming and diving, boys golf, boys tennis, boys volleyball, girls beach volleyball, and a surf team.

Schedules are posted at slvathletics.org. They're organized by season and include dates, levels, opponents, and mapped venues. The site also offers a subscription option for game reminders and links to NFHS Network for streamed games.

The school's sports page hosts the athlete packet and links for each team. The athletics site links to the Santa Cruz Coast Athletic League, and the school maintains CCS and CIF state championship pages. SLV High also publishes a weekly sports newsletter. We don't reprint game schedules here because they change weekly, and a stale schedule is worse than no schedule.

Enrolling, and moving between schools

New students. Contact the registrar at your assigned school to establish pre-enrollment status. Once approved, the registrar emails instructions for completing registration online. The district asks families to finish it within a week.

You'll need proof of your child's age, immunization records, proof of address, and, for TK through first grade, an oral health assessment. Kindergartners must be five by September 1. TK students must turn four before that date. The enrollment page has the packets and registrar contacts.

Returning families. The PowerSchool enrollment portal opens in the spring for annual updates. The district notifies families by letter or email. Keep emergency contacts and phone numbers current because the district uses that record when something goes wrong.

Transfers. An intradistrict transfer moves a student between SLVUSD elementary schools, such as from Boulder Creek Elementary to SLV Elementary. It uses an Application for Open Enrollment and only needs to be filed once during a student's school career unless the address changes.

An interdistrict transfer crosses district lines in either direction. It uses the countywide request form. SLVUSD reviews the request before forwarding an approved application to the receiving district.

The window for the following school year opens in early January. Decisions come back within roughly two to four weeks, depending on the filing date. Direct questions to Instructional Services at 831-336-8852 extension 131. The transfer page has the forms.

Getting there from Boulder Creek

District busing is limited. The bus information page lists four named routes. Only the Bunther bus serves Boulder Creek Elementary, along with SLV Middle and the charter. The other three routes run from SLV Elementary and points south.

Bus passes are available annually or by semester, one-way or round trip. Ticket books are available for occasional riders. The most recent posted fee list ran $220 for an annual round-trip pass and $20 for a book of twenty tickets. Students with severe disabilities under an IEP are exempt from fees. Families receiving county assistance can apply for a free pass using form T-3. Call the transportation office at 831-336-2223.

Two options fill the gaps. K-12 students ride Santa Cruz METRO free under Youth Cruz Free. Route 35 runs along the Highway 9 corridor past the Felton campus. Our transit guide covers the service in detail.

Everyone else drives. Highway 9 thickens between 7:30 and 8:15 and again at pickup. If the road is new to you, read driving the mountain roads before your first week.

The dates that move your week

The 2026-27 school year started Thursday, August 6, 2026, and ends Thursday, June 3, 2027. It includes 180 instructional days. Three parts of the calendar require particular attention:

  • Back-to-school nights are spread across a week and a half in August: SLV Middle on the 12th, SLV High on the 13th, the charter's Nature Academy on the 18th, and both Boulder Creek Elementary and SLV Elementary on the 20th.
  • Early-out Wednesdays happen at the elementary schools every week except October 21, 2026. Boulder Creek Elementary releases at 1:15 p.m., and SLV Elementary releases at 1:25 p.m. Middle and high school early-outs fall on scattered Mondays instead. The middle school releases at 1:40, and the high school releases at 2:01.
  • Parent-teacher conference week at the elementary schools runs from October 19 to 23, 2026. SLV Elementary releases at noon that week.

Grades follow trimesters in K-5 and semesters in grades 6-12. The district publishes both reporting calendars on the same sheet. The district calendar page is the authority if anything changes. Each school also posts its own calendar.

How the district talks to you

There's no single information feed. Grades, records, and annual re-registration are in the PowerSchool parent portal.

Day-to-day news comes from the school, not the district. Boulder Creek Elementary sends Smore newsletters and posts news on its site. SLV High publishes Cougar Weekly and a separate weekly sports newsletter. The district website carries the calendar, department pages, and board information.

A missing school email is almost always caused by a wrong address in PowerSchool. The school office can correct it.

Frequently asked questions

Which high school do Boulder Creek students attend?

San Lorenzo Valley High School at 7105 Highway 9 in Felton, the valley's only comprehensive high school. Coast Redwood High School, the charter's hybrid independent study program in Ben Lomond, is the district-run alternative.

How many schools does SLVUSD have?

Five: Boulder Creek Elementary, San Lorenzo Valley Elementary, SLV Middle, SLV High, and SLV Charter School. The charter runs several distinct programs, including Nature Academy and Coast Redwood High School.

Is there a school bus from Boulder Creek?

Yes, one. The Bunther route serves Boulder Creek Elementary along with SLV Middle and the charter. Passes are sold annually or by semester, with a fee-waiver path for qualifying families. Call transportation at 831-336-2223 to confirm this year's stops and times.

How do I switch my child from one valley elementary school to the other?

That's an intradistrict transfer. File an Application for Open Enrollment with Instructional Services, 831-336-8852 extension 131. It only needs to be filed once unless your address changes.

Where do I find SLV High sports schedules?

At slvathletics.org, which lists every team by season with venues and times and offers game reminders by subscription. Schedules change from week to week, so use the source instead of a printed list.

Details here come from SLVUSD, the individual school sites, and Santa Cruz METRO, all linked above. Dates and fees change, so confirm anything time-sensitive with the district before relying on it. Spot something out of date? Tell us. Last reviewed August 5, 2026.

Once school is handled, the rest of the week is covered in kids' activities around Boulder Creek, and the wider support list is in our family resources guide.

kids-activities-boulder-creek.title: Kids' Activities in and Around Boulder Creek, Season by Season
kids-activities-boulder-creek.html:
The short version

  • The recreation district is the engine. BCRPD runs the widest slate of kids' programming in town, from toddler tumbling to a Friday teen night, out of the Downtown Rec Center and the Bear Creek Community Center.
  • Free every week: storytime and a playgroup at the library branch on West Park Avenue, plus a school-age STEAM program.
  • Fall is sign-up season. Rec district enrichment sessions start the week school does, 4-H youth enrollment opened August 3, and basketball evaluations land in early November.
  • Sports mean a drive. Little League and SLV Hoops are valley-wide organizations that play mostly down the road, not in town.
  • Winter is indoor and improvised. The pool closes in late September and the library becomes the reliable warm room.

Boulder Creek has no kids' activity center, no mall, and no chain gym with a childcare room. Most organized options come through a recreation district that offers a lot for a town this size, a small library branch with regular programming, and a handful of valley-wide organizations you join rather than drop into. Once you know the four or five doors, the year is easier to plan.

We're in the thick of this exact season of life: our daughter is just starting rec department programs this month, learning to walk on the same downtown sidewalks her parents grew up on. The doors below are the ones we're walking through ourselves.

Schedules move every session, so treat the organizer's link as the truth and this page as the map. For summer, our summer camps guide goes deeper than this one does.

Start with the recreation district

The Boulder Creek Recreation and Park District is where most of the town's organized kid activity lives. Keep both locations handy: the Downtown Rec Center at 13333 Middleton Avenue, 831-338-4144, open Tuesday to Friday 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., and the Bear Creek Community Center at 15685 Forest Hill Drive, 831-703-4135, open Tuesday through Sunday with hours that vary.

The district's youth programs page is the live catalog, and it turns over by session. The main options are:

  • Movement classes, year-round. A tumbling and dance ladder that starts with a parent-participation class for babies and toddlers and climbs through ninja and tumbling classes into a cheer-and-dance group for kids up to about fourteen.
  • After-school enrichment, in six-week sessions from August through December. Recent sessions have included LEGO robotics, an art lab, a cooking class, an indoor adventure gym, and a sports club. Several offer a walk-down from Boulder Creek Elementary, which is the detail that makes them workable for a working parent.
  • Preschool-age programs. Little Explorers runs play-based preschool prep on weekday mornings. CIRCLE runs an enrichment program for three to five year olds out of South Street Centre.
  • A teen option. The Hangout is a Friday evening drop-in for kids twelve and up downtown, with a small door fee and pizza.

Registration runs through the district's online forms, linked from that page. Sessions fill, particularly anything with a walk-down.

The outdoor programs at Bear Creek

Three nature programs run out of the Bear Creek Community Center and register through enchantedlittleforestfriends.com rather than the rec district's forms.

Enchanted Little Forest Friends is an outdoor, play-based program for roughly ages two to five, two mornings a week, sold in fall, winter, and spring sessions. Adventure Fridays takes a slightly older group, about four to ten, out for a full Friday morning at Bear Creek and off-site locations. TRAIL Guides runs a few weeks in the fall for eleven to fifteen year olds and includes CPR and first aid certification. It's the closest thing the valley has to a babysitting course.

For homeschooling families, the Santa Cruz Mountains Learning Collective runs a two-day-a-week K-5 enrichment program on a school-year commitment.

The library branch, which is free

The Boulder Creek branch of Santa Cruz Public Libraries sits at 13390 West Park Avenue, 831-427-7703, open Monday through Thursday 10 to 6, Friday 11 to 5, and Saturday 10 to 5. Its recurring kids' lineup is free and needs no advance signup:

  • Toddler and Preschool Storytime, Wednesday mornings in the community room.
  • Discovery Zone Playgroup, Friday mornings, free play for young children with a participating adult, with come-and-go timing that suits a nap schedule.
  • Make & Explore, a STEAM program for school-age kids, plus periodic LEGO robotics sessions.
  • R.E.A.D., free one-on-one reading help for grades one through twelve, by appointment.

Summer brings a reading program and visiting performers. The rest of the year the branch is quieter and easier. Check the branch events calendar before leaving, because rooms and times shift.

Sports, and where they happen

Team sports are organized at the valley level, not the town level. For most families, that means signing up in Boulder Creek and driving to Felton or Ben Lomond.

Baseball and softball. San Lorenzo Valley Little League covers the valley towns including Boulder Creek, with boundaries, divisions, and registration windows posted at slvlittleleague.com. Registration opens in the winter for a spring season, and proof of residence or school attendance inside the league boundary is part of signing up.

Basketball. SLV Hoops, run by the Boulder Creek nonprofit SLV Youth, serves second grade through middle school in boys' and girls' divisions, with skill evaluations in early November and a winter season. SLV Youth also backs Santa Cruz SPIN, a high school softball program, and suspended its flag football program in 2024 for lack of coaches. Valley youth sports depend on parents to keep them running.

Gyms and music schools down the valley are listed in our local directory under Education and Childcare.

Scouts and 4-H

Both are year-long commitments rather than drop-ins, and both have deep roots here.

Scouting. Troop 623 has served the San Lorenzo Valley since the Kiwanis of San Lorenzo Valley and Scotts Valley chartered it in 1945, and it belongs to the Silicon Valley Monterey Bay Council. Contacts and joining information are at troop623.org, and a Cub Scout unit for elementary ages runs alongside it. If that contact page has gone stale, beascout.scouting.org lists currently chartered units by ZIP code.

4-H. The valley's club is Quail Creek 4-H, based in Boulder Creek, at quailcreek4hclub@gmail.com. Its feature projects are community service, a club fair booth, sheep, and swine. Members can also join countywide projects in poultry, rabbits, sewing, ag business, and shooting sports hosted by other clubs. 4-H takes youth aged five to eighteen and runs a program year from July 1 to June 30. Youth enrollment for this year opened August 3, 2026, and anyone showing at the county fair needs to be enrolled by August 31. The county office is at 831-205-3180, and the join page covers fees and the fee waiver.

Summer, briefly

Summer has more options than any other season. The Bear Creek pool at 15685 Forest Hill Drive ran June 6 through September 27 for the 2026 season, with recreational swim most afternoons, adult swim mornings and evenings, and Mondays closed. Passes and lessons are posted on the pool page.

Camps range from the rec district's own day camps to the two overnight camps on Highway 9 north of town. The summer camps and kids' classes guide covers registration timing, scholarships, and the camps down the valley.

Fall and winter, when it rains

Late September changes the calculation. The pool closes, the light goes early, and outdoor plans stop being reliable. These options hold up:

  • The library branch, warm, free, and open six days a week.
  • The rec district's indoor sessions, built for this stretch of the year and running through mid-December.
  • Basketball season, the main organized winter sport for elementary and middle school kids here.
  • Town events, which cluster in fall and winter: see Halloween downtown and the holiday season.
  • Down-the-hill days. Family day trips is built for rainy Saturdays, and a day in Boulder Creek with kids covers the in-town version.

Frequently asked questions

What can kids do in Boulder Creek for free?

The library branch on West Park Avenue runs a weekly storytime, a Friday playgroup, and a school-age STEAM program, all free and all without advance registration. The town's parks and playgrounds, including Junction Park a block off downtown, cost nothing and are open sunrise to sunset.

Where do kids play sports in the San Lorenzo Valley?

Kids play through valley-wide organizations rather than town teams. San Lorenzo Valley Little League handles baseball and softball, with winter registration for a spring season. SLV Hoops runs winter basketball from second grade through middle school. Both play mostly at fields and gyms down the valley.

Is there a 4-H club in Boulder Creek?

Yes. Quail Creek 4-H is the valley's club. The 4-H year runs July 1 through June 30, youth enrollment for the current year opened August 3, and anyone showing at the county fair needs to be enrolled by August 31. The county office is at 831-205-3180.

What is there for teenagers?

There is less than there is for younger kids, which is what a town this size supports. The rec district's Friday-evening Hangout takes twelve and up. TRAIL Guides certifies eleven to fifteen year olds in CPR and first aid in the fall. Scouts and 4-H both run through high school, and SLV High's athletics and arts programs carry most of the rest.

When is the Boulder Creek pool open?

Seasonally. The Bear Creek pool ran June 6 to September 27 in 2026, closed Mondays, with recreational swim most afternoons. Confirm the current season and hours with the recreation district before you go.

Programs, sessions, and fees here come from the recreation district, Santa Cruz Public Libraries, the leagues, and county 4-H, all linked above, and all of them change by season. Confirm through the organizer before you plan around anything. For the school-day bookends, see after-school care in Boulder Creek. Spot something out of date? Tell us. Last reviewed August 12, 2026.

moving-to-boulder-creek.title: Moving to Boulder Creek: What to Know Before You Commit
moving-to-boulder-creek.html:
The short version

  • One road carries everything. Highway 9 is the way in, the way out, the school bus route, and the evacuation route. Storms and slides close it, and there's no quick detour.
  • Your house may be its own utility. Much of the valley uses delivered propane, private wells, and septic systems instead of gas mains, district water, and sewer. Confirm every service parcel by parcel before you write an offer.
  • Outages are routine. Plan for them the way you would plan for winter anywhere else.
  • Fire insurance can end a deal. Get a real quote for the specific address early in escrow, not the week before closing.
  • Coverage is address-specific. Cell signal and internet vary street by street. Treat “high speed available” in a listing as a claim to verify.
  • The commute is real. Allow roughly 30 minutes to Santa Cruz on a good day and 40 to 50 minutes to San Jose. A bad day on Highway 9 or Highway 17 can double either trip.

People who stay tend to like these systems or accept them. You learn where the propane tank gauge is. You keep a case of water and a headlamp somewhere easy to find. You batch errands. You remember that the hardware store closes at five.

That list isn't hypothetical; it's my house. Lifelong resident, and the propane gauge, the stored water, the batched errands, and the five o'clock hardware run are all real fixtures of the calendar. None of it feels like hardship from the inside. It feels like knowing your home.

People who leave are usually worn down by the logistics, not the redwoods. An insurance renewal doubles. A well pump quits during a four-day outage. A commute that looked manageable on a Sunday test drive feels different at 7:15 on a Tuesday in February. These conditions aren't hidden, but they rarely appear in the listing.

This guide covers the operational parts of living here that a property tour won't show you. If you're still deciding whether to move, start with the trade-offs of living in Boulder Creek. If you've already signed, the new resident quick-start covers week one.

Highway 9 is the infrastructure

Boulder Creek sits on State Route 9. The Regional Transportation Commission treats it as both the valley’s main street and its regional connector. It runs from Highway 1 in Santa Cruz through Felton, Ben Lomond and Brookdale, then continues toward Los Gatos. The commission has a dedicated Highway 9 program for exactly this reason.

One road failure can reorganize your day. A downed redwood, slide, or crash can close the highway without a useful alternate route. Bear Creek Road and Empire Grade are longer, narrower, and often closed during the same storm. Our guides to Highway 9 in winter storms and driving mountain roads cover the driving conditions. The mountain status page tracks closures as they happen.

Before you commit, drive the route you would use. Do it in the rain if you can. Look closely at how the prospective driveway meets the road. Steep, unpaved, and shared driveways are common here, and they carry their own long-term expenses.

Many houses here are their own utility company

This is one of the largest adjustments for people moving from a city. It can also create expensive problems after closing if you don't verify each service first.

Gas. Some addresses have PG&E natural gas service. Many mountain properties use delivered propane instead. That means a tank on the property, a supplier you choose, and a delivery schedule you manage. Don't infer the fuel source from the appliances. Ask PG&E what's connected at the address.

Water. Most homes in town are customers of the San Lorenzo Valley Water District. The district has served the valley since 1941 and covers Boulder Creek, Brookdale, Ben Lomond, Lompico, Zayante, Felton and more through over 7,900 connections. Outlying parcels use private wells or small shared systems. With a well, the pump, testing, treatment, and repairs are your responsibility.

Waste. Most properties treat wastewater on-site with a septic system permitted and overseen by Santa Cruz County Environmental Health. A portion of town near the core uses the county’s CSA 7 sewer instead. Its annual charge appears on the property tax bill. Our septic basics guide explains what you're inheriting. Read it before the inspection contingency expires.

Trash. GreenWaste Recovery holds the curbside collection franchise. Under the county’s universal service requirement, every developed property in the unincorporated county must subscribe or register as a self-hauler. The compliance deadline is November 1, 2026, with escalating fines after that.

Our utilities guide maps who serves what and includes phone numbers.

Power outages are a season, not an event

Power goes out here. Storms bring down lines, and PG&E can call a Public Safety Power Shutoff during high fire-risk weather. A few days without power in Boulder Creek is treated more like a weekend to manage than a crisis.

Preparation makes the difference. If you've a well, no power means no water, so you need stored water. If you work from home, home internet and cordless phones also stop working without power. Read the power outage plan and winter storm checklist before your first winter. The twenty-year rainfall record shows what a wet year looks like here.

Fire insurance is the hurdle that stops sales

Insurance is the part of a mountain purchase most likely to fail. The problem often appears late, when the buyer learns the premium or discovers that no admitted carrier will write the address. Start this work during the first week of escrow.

Our guide to fire insurance in the Santa Cruz Mountains explains how the FAIR Plan and DIC wrap policies work together, why you should re-shop the regular market every year, and how home hardening relates to discounts. Read it before making an offer. Get a written quote for the specific address rather than relying on a neighborhood estimate. Two houses a mile apart can have very different prices.

Wildfire risk also requires preparation. Sign up for CruzAware alerts on day one and read our evacuation guide.

Cell service and internet are address-by-address

There's no single answer to whether a property has service. Coverage varies by canyon, ridge, and sometimes by room.

Start with two checks. Enter the exact address in the FCC National Broadband Map. It shows every provider reporting home internet and mobile service at that location. Treat those results as claims to verify with each carrier.

Then use your own phone in the driveway and on the back deck. Watch the bars. Ask the nearest neighbors what service they use and how it performs during a storm. Their experience is more useful than a coverage map.

If you work remotely, choose an outage fallback before you need it. Many households use a cell hotspot as a backup, but that only works if the signal at the house is reliable.

The commute, stated plainly

On a good day, allow about 30 minutes to Santa Cruz, 40 to 50 minutes to San Jose by way of Highway 9 and Highway 17, and 50 to 60 minutes toward Redwood City. These are the working estimates used on our job board, and they hold up in ordinary conditions.

They're good-day numbers. Highway 17 has its own backups. Winter weather or a tree across Highway 9 can make any trip much longer. Test the commute by driving your route at your normal hour on a weekday and during the season you dread.

A car isn't the only option. Santa Cruz METRO’s Route 35 runs along Highway 9 to downtown Santa Cruz seven days a week, with a weekday express. K-12 and college students ride free. Our public transportation guide covers routes, fares, and the transfer to the Highway 17 Express for San Jose.

Schools, health care, and the rest of daily life

The public school district is San Lorenzo Valley Unified. It operates the valley’s elementary schools, middle school, high school, and its own bus routes. Start with our guide to schools, daycare and preschool in the valley. Confirm boundaries and enrollment steps for a specific address through the district’s own site.

Two markets, a pharmacy and a hardware store cover most daily needs. They're mapped in our essential shops guide. Urgent care and hospitals are down the highway, as explained in our healthcare guide.

The list of places for dinner is short. See where to eat and pizza. A big-box run means going to Scotts Valley or Santa Cruz, so most residents learn to batch those errands.

What to check before you sign

Check these items in the order most likely to prevent trouble:

  • Insurance quote for the exact address, in writing, in the first week of escrow.
  • Water source: district connection or private well, confirmed with the district or well records, not the listing.
  • Wastewater: septic system age, last pumping, permit history and any county compliance items, or sewer connection and its annual charge.
  • Gas: propane or PG&E natural gas, and if propane, whether the tank is owned or rented.
  • Access: who maintains the driveway and private road, and what that costs each year.
  • Trees: hazard trees near the house and the defensible space work already completed or overdue.
  • Signal: your own phone while standing on the property, plus the FCC map.
  • Drainage: where water goes during a real storm, as explained in our culverts and drainage guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

How far is Boulder Creek from Santa Cruz?

Downtown Santa Cruz is roughly 17 miles down Highway 9 through Brookdale, Ben Lomond and Felton. The drive takes about 30 minutes in ordinary conditions. Treat both figures as approximate. Highway 9 is a two-lane mountain road, and traffic, weather, or a closure can make the trip considerably longer. Santa Cruz METRO Route 35 makes the same trip by bus seven days a week.

Does Boulder Creek have natural gas?

Some addresses do, and many do not. A large share of valley properties use delivered propane for heating and cooking. This requires an on-site tank and a private supplier. Don't infer the fuel source from the appliances. Ask PG&E what's connected at the specific address before buying anything that requires one fuel or the other.

Is Boulder Creek on city water and sewer?

Most properties don't have city-style water and sewer service. Most homes in town are customers of the San Lorenzo Valley Water District. Outlying parcels use private wells. Most properties treat wastewater with a septic system rather than a sewer. A portion of town near the core uses the county’s CSA 7 sewer. Confirm each service parcel by parcel.

How often does the power go out in Boulder Creek?

Often enough that every household needs a plan. Winter storms bring down lines, and PG&E can call a Public Safety Power Shutoff during high fire-risk weather. We don't publish an outage-frequency figure because it varies by circuit and year, and we've no first-party source for one. Ask the neighbors on your road and read our power outage plan.

Can I get reliable internet in Boulder Creek?

Many addresses have reliable service. Some barely have service. Availability changes street by street. Check the exact address on the FCC National Broadband Map, confirm the result with each provider’s address checker, and ask the nearest neighbors how their connection performs during winter. If remote work makes the move possible, complete this check before making an offer.

Is Boulder Creek a good place to raise kids?

Many families think so. The valley has its own school district, parks, summer camps and a tight-knit community. Families also face drive time to almost everything, one road out, and fewer after-school options than a suburb offers. Our family resources guide and schools guide are the practical starting points.

Last reviewed August 12, 2026. Service territories, road conditions, insurance rules and district boundaries change, and almost everything on this page is parcel-specific. Confirm anything decision-critical with the provider, agency, or a licensed professional before you rely on it.

Ready to look? Our rentals board tracks local listings as they come up, the job board refreshes daily, and the Residents guide collects utilities, permits and county contacts in one place. For the financial side of the decision, see what it costs to live in Boulder Creek.

cost-of-living-boulder-creek.title: What It Costs to Live in Boulder Creek
cost-of-living-boulder-creek.html:
Living in Boulder Creek is expensive. The costs that most often strain a budget are water, insurance, propane, commuting, and mountain property maintenance. The figures below are sourced and dated. Use each one as a starting point for your own quote.

The short version

  • Sales tax here is 9.50%. Boulder Creek is unincorporated, so it takes the Santa Cruz County unincorporated rate, listed by the CDTFA at 9.500% effective July 1, 2026, against 9.750% in the cities of Santa Cruz and Scotts Valley.
  • Property tax runs about 1.15% of assessed value. San Lorenzo Valley tax rate areas totaled 1.145785% for 2025-26 in the county Auditor-Controller's tax rate book: the 1% Proposition 13 base plus school and college bonds.
  • Rent is thin and expensive. The three listings on our rentals board on August 5, 2026 ran $3,600 to $4,500 a month. That's a snapshot, not an average.
  • Water has a floor. A district customer on a standard 3/4 inch meter pays about $75 a month in fixed charges before using a drop.
  • Propane has no published price. No agency publishes a California residential rate, so call three suppliers.
  • The commute is a line item. At the IRS rate of 76 cents a mile, a 35-mile round trip to Santa Cruz runs about $27 a day all in.

People don't move to the Santa Cruz Mountains for cheap living. Some of the largest expenses arrive unevenly, including an insurance premium that behaves like a second mortgage payment or a propane delivery that lands in January.

Rent: a small market, and the listings prove it

On August 5, 2026, our rentals board carried three active listings in the upper valley: a 2-bedroom on Highway 9 in Boulder Creek at $3,600 a month, a 4-bedroom in Brookdale at $4,300, and a 3-bedroom in Ben Lomond at $4,500. All three were whole houses from property managers, available immediately.

The listing count matters as much as the prices. Three listings can't establish a typical rent. They do show that inventory is thin and that much of the available housing consists of whole single-family houses rather than apartments. Plenty of valley rentals never reach a listing site at all. Budget for a longer search.

Buying: the market is defined by its range, not its median

Published estimates for Boulder Creek differ by well over $100,000 depending on who is counting and what they count. The range within town is wider still, so a single median can mislead buyers.

A small cabin on a steep, shady lot with a tired septic system and a shared driveway is a different purchase from a rebuilt house on a flat, sunny parcel with district water and county road frontage. Condition, sun, water source, and access move prices here more than square footage does. Our guide to the trade-offs of living in Boulder Creek includes the price-range estimates we've sourced, with their dates.

Insurance and deferred mountain maintenance are the two costs most likely to catch buyers short. Get a written insurance quote for the specific address in the first week of escrow. Read our fire insurance guide before you make an offer.

Property tax: the 1% is only the start

Proposition 13 sets the basic framework. The county Auditor-Controller describes it as capping property tax rates at 1 percent and holding value increases to "no more than 2% unless there is a change in ownership or new construction." A purchase resets the assessment to the purchase price.

Voter-approved bonds are added to the 1% rate. In the county's 2025-26 property tax rate book, San Lorenzo Valley tax rate areas (the 90 series) came to 1.145785% of assessed value: the 1% general rate, seven San Lorenzo Valley school district bonds, and five Cabrillo College bonds. On an $800,000 assessed value that's about $9,170 a year, and on $600,000, about $6,875.

Fixed charges can also appear on the same bill:

  • Sewer, if you're on it. Properties on the county's CSA 7 Boulder Creek Sanitation sewer were charged $2,813.45 per single-family dwelling for 2025-26, up from $2,747.51 the year before, per the same tax rate book. Condominiums were $2,536.55.
  • Septic management. The county's septic management service areas charged $35.56 and $24.69 per parcel for 2025-26.
  • One relief worth claiming. The Assessor's Homeowners' Exemption takes $7,000 off the assessed value of an owner-occupied home, worth roughly $80 a year at the valley's rate. File by February 15 for the full amount.

Tax rate areas are parcel-specific, so confirm the rate for yours. When you buy, expect a supplemental bill covering the difference between the seller's assessment and your new one.

Sales tax: 9.50%

Boulder Creek is unincorporated, so purchases here use the county's unincorporated rate. The California Department of Tax and Fee Administration's city and county rate table, effective July 1, 2026, lists Santa Cruz County Unincorporated Area at 9.500%. Boulder Creek doesn't appear by name because the department doesn't list unincorporated communities separately.

The same table puts the cities of Santa Cruz and Scotts Valley at 9.750%, making the rate in Boulder Creek a quarter point lower. Rates change when local measures pass, so check the table before relying on this figure.

Utilities: where the fixed costs hide

Water, if you're a district customer. The San Lorenzo Valley Water District's current rate schedule sets monthly charges for a 5/8 or 3/4 inch meter, the residential standard, at $56.55 service, $9.01 capital, and a $9.67 fire surcharge. That comes to about $75 a month before you use any water. Usage is billed per unit, with one unit equal to 100 cubic feet or 748 gallons: $10.23 for the first 4 units, $13.88 for units 5 through 8, and $19.87 above that. A household using 5 units lands near $130 all in. Those rates apply to usage after January 1, 2026. The same schedule raises the service charge to $60.51 and tier one to $10.95 for usage after January 1, 2027.

Water, if you're on a well. There's no bill and no district to call. Budget for testing, treatment, and pump repairs instead.

Trash, recycling and organics. GreenWaste Recovery's residential rates for unincorporated Santa Cruz County, effective July 1, 2026, run $29.37 a month for a 20-gallon garbage cart, $40.55 for 32 gallons, $81.00 for 64 gallons and $121.42 for 96 gallons. A recyclables cart and an organics cart are included. Lifeline rates are available to qualifying customers, and service is no longer optional in the unincorporated county.

Electricity. Your PG&E bill depends on your rate plan, baseline territory, and usage, so a general article can't quote it for you. For scale, the U.S. Energy Information Administration put the average residential price in California at 33.25 cents per kilowatthour in May 2026. Multiply that rate by the kilowatthours on your own bill. Households running a well pump, electric heat, or a septic pump sit well above a suburban average.

Propane. There's no published California residential propane price to cite. The federal weekly residential propane survey covers the East Coast, Midwest, Gulf Coast and Rocky Mountain regions, but not the West Coast. The local market is private and competitive, so the price is whatever you negotiate. Call three suppliers and get the current per-gallon price in writing. Ask separately about tank rental versus ownership, delivery minimums, and automatic fill through winter.

Insurance. For most mountain households, insurance is the largest and most volatile line in the budget. It deserves its own page rather than a general number here. See fire insurance in the Santa Cruz Mountains.

The commute costs more than gas

If you drive over the hill or down to the coast for work, account for the full cost. The IRS sets a standard mileage rate of 76 cents a mile for business driving from July 1 through December 31, 2026. That rate is meant to capture the whole cost of running a car, not just fuel. A 35-mile round trip to Santa Cruz works out to about $27 a day, or roughly $530 a month at 20 workdays. Highway 17 to San Jose is far more.

Fuel is the smaller share, but it's the expense you pay each week. The EIA put California's average regular retail gasoline price at $5.495 a gallon in the week ending August 3, 2026.

METRO Route 35 runs down Highway 9 to Santa Cruz seven days a week, and K-12 and college students ride free. Our public transportation guide has fares and the Highway 17 Express connection.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the sales tax rate in Boulder Creek?

9.50%. Boulder Creek is unincorporated, so it uses the Santa Cruz County unincorporated rate, listed by the CDTFA at 9.500% effective July 1, 2026. The cities of Santa Cruz and Scotts Valley charge 9.750%. Rates change when local measures pass, so confirm the current figure on the department's own table.

What is the property tax rate in Boulder Creek?

About 1.15% of assessed value. San Lorenzo Valley tax rate areas totaled 1.145785% for 2025-26: the 1% Proposition 13 base plus San Lorenzo Valley school district and Cabrillo College bonds. Fixed charges such as the CSA 7 sewer charge are added on top, and rates are parcel-specific.

How much is rent in Boulder Creek?

The three listings on our rentals board on August 5, 2026 ran $3,600 to $4,500 a month. All were whole single-family houses. This is a snapshot of a thin market rather than an average, and many valley rentals never get listed publicly at all.

How much is the water bill in Boulder Creek?

For San Lorenzo Valley Water District customers on a standard 5/8 or 3/4 inch meter, fixed monthly charges total about $75 before any usage. Water runs $10.23 per 100 cubic feet in the first tier, so a household using 5 units lands near $130. Homes on private wells pay no bill and cover their own pump and testing.

Is Boulder Creek cheaper than Santa Cruz?

Some costs are lower and others are higher. Sales tax is a quarter point lower here, and housing has run below coastal Santa Cruz prices. Mountain households also carry higher insurance, higher commute costs, propane instead of piped gas, and upkeep that a city lot doesn't demand.

What is the biggest unexpected cost of living in Boulder Creek?

Fire insurance is the cost most likely to reorder a household budget, so quote it first. Other substantial costs come with trees, slopes, and private roads: defensible space, tree removal, driveway repair, drainage, and septic service.

Last reviewed August 5, 2026. Every figure here carries the date and source it came from, and all of them change. Confirm rates with the agency or provider before you decide anything. Nothing here is financial, tax, or insurance advice.

Start with moving to Boulder Creek for what's operationally different up here, and the utilities guide for who serves what.

food-delivery-boulder-creek.title: What Food Delivery Works in Boulder Creek
food-delivery-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek has food delivery. DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub all serve town addresses and outlying roads. Grocery delivery works here too. The options are spread across several apps, so this guide covers what each one carries, which pizzerias deliver, where groceries come from, and which local kitchens offer advance ordering for pickup.

Here's how I know what delivers up here. When our baby arrived, friends and coworkers sent DoorDash gift cards, the mountain version of a meal train, since casserole drop-offs don't quite work when everyone lives twenty minutes up a winding road. We worked through every local place that delivers, most of them more than once.

The short version

  • All three apps serve Boulder Creek: DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub.
  • In town, River Dogs is on DoorDash, and Taqueria Los Gallos on Central Avenue is on Uber Eats.
  • Pizza arrives three ways: Round Table in Felton through its own ordering page, The Pizza Series through DoorDash, and Mountain Mike's through Grubhub.
  • For groceries, Safeway, Costco, and Nob Hill deliver through Instacart and DoorDash. Imperfect Foods also delivers its boxes here. Amazon Fresh doesn't serve Boulder Creek.
  • Restaurant rosters change with the weather, business hours, and available drivers. The app's answer for your address when you place the order is the final word.

On DoorDash

Boulder Creek has one local DoorDash option: River Dogs, the outdoor hot dog stand on Forest Street.

The app also brings orders up from Brookdale, Ben Lomond, Felton, and Scotts Valley:

  • Brookdale Diner is at 11570 Highway 9 in Brookdale. Its in-house delivery serves rooms inside the Lodge. DoorDash is the option for delivery to your house.
  • Paleteria Los Freseros is a new paleta shop in Ben Lomond with no website yet.
  • Felton options include Empire Grill, The Grove bakery and cafe, and Taqueria Vallarta.
  • Scotts Valley options include Kao Sook Thai, Maya Mexican, Laughing Monk Brewing, Canton Restaurant, House of Bagels, Taqueria Los Gallos' Scotts Valley location, Peet's, Starbucks, and Chipotle.

The standout of our gift-card era was Kao Sook. The pineapple fried rice is refreshing, the sweet tang balancing the salt, and the yellow curry with extra potatoes carries just the right amount of kick. The mango sticky rice is worth the delivery fee even if it's the only thing you order.

On Uber Eats

In Boulder Creek, Uber Eats carries Taqueria Los Gallos at 13070 Central Avenue.

From Scotts Valley, the roster includes Ambrosia India Bistro, Rumble Fish, Erik's DeliCafe, Jia Tella's, La Chimichanga Cantina, Soul Sweets Tea House, Maya Mexican, and Canton Restaurant.

Uber Eats also lists several Santa Cruz restaurants for Boulder Creek delivery: The Habit Burger Grill, Ike's Love & Sandwiches, Fusion Fare, Noodle Time, and Back Nine Grill & Bar.

On Grubhub

Grubhub's Boulder Creek options come from Scotts Valley. The list includes Mountain Mike's Pizza, Erik's DeliCafe, Starbucks, Subway, Togo's, Chipotle, La Chimichanga, and Jamba.

Pizza delivery

Three pizzerias deliver to Boulder Creek, each through a different ordering route.

Round Table's Felton store delivers through its own ordering page. The Pizza Series in Scotts Valley delivers through DoorDash. Mountain Mike's in Scotts Valley delivers through Grubhub.

Redwood Pizzeria in Felton doesn't deliver to Boulder Creek. It's a dine-in or pickup trip. For more detail, including what closed downtown, see our pizza guide.

Order ahead, pick up downtown

Two local food businesses take advance orders for pickup in downtown Boulder Creek.

Creative Heart Kitchen offers a weekly prepared-meal menu with pickup in Boulder Creek, Brookdale, and Ben Lomond. Orders close days ahead, making this a Sunday decision about Wednesday dinner.

Butter Late Than Never bakes custom cookie orders and meets customers downtown. Because these are custom orders, allow a couple of days between ordering and pickup.

Ordering for pickup

Several Boulder Creek restaurants accept online orders for pickup at the restaurant. Red Pearl operates this way, and so has The Sawmill, though the Sawmill is expected to close temporarily for renovations after August 14, 2026, so check before counting on it. Neither delivers.

Downtown is a short drive from most of town. Pickup also remains an option when the power is out.

Groceries

Safeway in Felton, Costco, and Nob Hill deliver to Boulder Creek through Instacart and DoorDash. Safeway also provides its own delivery and DriveUp & Go pickup from the Graham Hill Road store, 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Imperfect Foods delivers produce-and-pantry boxes here as well. In town, Wild Roots and Johnnie's are in-store shopping options.

When the list changes

Delivery coverage is determined one address at a time, based partly on which drivers are online. Storms can shrink the service area. A closure on Highway 9 can remove delivery options for the evening.

If an app declines your address, try the restaurant's own phone line. It's often the better route.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which delivery apps work in Boulder Creek?

DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub all serve Boulder Creek, including the outlying roads. Each app carries a different group of restaurants, so it's worth checking more than one.

Who delivers pizza to Boulder Creek?

Round Table in Felton delivers through its own ordering page. The Pizza Series delivers through DoorDash, and Mountain Mike's delivers through Grubhub. Redwood Pizzeria doesn't deliver here. See our pizza guide.

Can I get groceries delivered in Boulder Creek?

Yes. Safeway, Costco, and Nob Hill deliver through Instacart and DoorDash. Safeway also delivers directly from its Felton store, and Imperfect Foods delivers here. Amazon Fresh doesn't serve Boulder Creek. Wild Roots and Johnnie's in town are in-store shopping.

Do any Boulder Creek restaurants deliver?

Yes, through the apps. River Dogs is on DoorDash, and Taqueria Los Gallos is on Uber Eats. No restaurant in town operates its own delivery driver. Creative Heart Kitchen and Butter Late Than Never accept advance orders for downtown pickup.

How current is this list?

The rosters are a snapshot from August 2026. They change with weather, business hours, and driver availability. If something here has changed, tell us and we'll fix it.

Last reviewed August 12, 2026. Business details follow each business's own page where one exists.

See also where to eat in Boulder Creek, the pizza guide, and the food and drink listings.

sawmill-boulder-creek.title: The Sawmill Restaurant & Alehouse: Boulder Creek's Yard Under the Redwoods
sawmill-boulder-creek.html:
The Sawmill is where a meal in Boulder Creek turns into an evening outdoors. It sits at 15520 Highway 9, a few minutes north of downtown and across the street from Garrahan Park, and it puts American fare and craft beer in a large open yard with a stage in it.

Status note (August 2026): the Sawmill is expected to close temporarily after service on Friday, August 14, 2026, for renovations. A reopening is planned, and community posts indicate the restaurant may return with a counter-service model, but the reopening date, incoming ownership, and final format haven't been publicly confirmed. We'll update this page as the picture firms up; in the meantime, call 831-610-8196 before planning a visit.

What kind of place it is

The restaurant describes itself as a place for "American fare, craft beers and an expansive outdoor area with a music stage," and that's the shape of it: burgers and pub food, beer on tap, and far more seating outside than a room its size would suggest. Its own Facebook page puts it more plainly still, as "casual dining with a beautiful outdoor area for on leash dogs and families."

That last part matters locally. Dogs on leash are welcome in the yard, which narrows the list of places in the valley you can bring one to dinner.

The menu

The owner supplied the current board (August 2026); prices move and specials rotate, so treat this as the shape of it.

  • Burgers, the center of the menu, built on half-pound Braveheart Black Angus beef ($15 to $21): the cheeseburger ($18), BBQ burger with an onion ring and bacon ($20), mushroom burger with Santa Cruz Fungi mushrooms and marsala ($20), bacon avo burger ($20), the Big Smack ($21), a chopped cheese ($18), single and double smash burgers ($15 and $19), a junior cheeseburger ($15), and chicken or shroom phillies ($15).
  • Appetizers ($12 to $15): wings in buffalo, dry rub, BBQ, or garlic parmesan ($14 and up), a beer-battered onion ring tower with logger sauce ($14), jalapeno poppers ($12), garlic and garlic-parmesan fries ($12), and tenders with fries ($15).
  • Sandwiches ($17 to $18): fried chicken on a buttermilk-marinated thigh, tri tip with bacon and cheddar, Cali chicken, pesto chicken, and a BLTA.
  • Salads and vegetarian ($10 to $18): a poached pear and candied walnut salad, arugula salad, iceberg wedge, Caesar, Baja salad, and a portobello burger, with veggie smash burgers and a veggie cheesesteak on the specials board.
  • Entrees: blackened salmon with dill sauce ($35), Baja fish tacos ($15 and up), and fish and chips ($15 and up).
  • Wraps ($17): BBQ, buffalo, and Baja.
  • Kids and dogs: a kids menu from butter noodles ($8) to a kids cheeseburger ($15), and a K9 menu of plain burgers and grilled chicken for the dog you brought.
  • Dessert: sundaes and a root beer float ($8), vegan cheesecake ($9), and a rotating cake or two.

The yard and the stage

The outdoor area is the draw, and it's the part of the restaurant its own site leads with. There's a stage out in the yard, and the Sawmill has run a long list of local and regional acts across it.

Whether a band is playing on the night you want to go is a separate question. The restaurant keeps an events page, but the newest show listed on it's several years old, so it's not a schedule to plan around. Its Facebook and Instagram are the channels that move.

Ordering, and the drive

There's online ordering on the Sawmill's site, running through Toast. It's for pickup at the restaurant. The Sawmill doesn't deliver, so takeout means a drive up Highway 9 either way.

The site doesn't publish hours, so here they are: 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily, except Wednesday, when the kitchen opens at 4 p.m. Call 831-610-8196 if you're cutting it close.

Hours and menus change. Go to the Sawmill's own site or call 831-610-8196 for anything time-sensitive.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Sawmill deliver?

No. Its online ordering is for pickup at the restaurant, and it's not on the delivery apps. See what food delivery works in Boulder Creek for what does reach town.

Can I bring my dog?

Yes, on leash, in the outdoor area.

Is there live music?

There's a stage in the yard and a history of shows on it. The restaurant's events page isn't current, so check its Facebook or Instagram for what's booked now.

What are the hours?

11 a.m. to 8 p.m. every day except Wednesday, when it opens at 4 p.m. The Sawmill doesn't post them on its own site, so call 831-610-8196 to confirm anything time-sensitive.

Where is it exactly?

15520 Highway 9, north of downtown Boulder Creek, across from Garrahan Park. It's a few minutes' drive up the road from the main block.

Last reviewed August 12, 2026. Details follow the restaurant's own site and social channels. Hours aren't published anywhere we can point to, so call.

taqueria-los-gallos-boulder-creek.title: Taqueria Los Gallos: The Sit-Down Taqueria on Central Avenue
taqueria-los-gallos-boulder-creek.html:
Taqueria Los Gallos is the taqueria you sit down in. It's at 13070 Central Avenue, in the middle of downtown Boulder Creek, and it serves tacos, burritos, and the rest of the standard order in a plain dining room rather than at a window.

That distinction is worth making because the town's other Mexican option, El Rey Leon, is a food truck parked further down the same street with outdoor seating. Los Gallos is the indoor one. On a wet February evening that's the whole difference.

Ordering, and the two locations

The same owners run Taqueria Los Gallos in Boulder Creek and the taqueria of the same name in Scotts Valley. If you're ordering through an app, the delivery listing that reaches a Boulder Creek address from the Boulder Creek kitchen is on Uber Eats. The DoorDash listing under that name is the Scotts Valley location.

Los Gallos and River Dogs are the only two Boulder Creek restaurants that any delivery app carries. Everything else in town is pickup or a table.

Hours

Open every day at 8:30 a.m. Monday through Friday it serves until 8:45 p.m.; Saturday and Sunday until 7:45 p.m. That makes it one of the latest kitchens in town, and one of the few places serving anything at all before 9 a.m. Hours change, so call 831-217-5000 to confirm before a special trip.

The menu

Los Gallos posts no menu online, so here is the shape of it. Prices are from August 2026 and will drift, there are weekly specials, and more items are on the board in person.

  • Tacos: regular soft taco ($5.49), crispy taco ($7.49), fish soft taco ($7.99), super soft taco ($8.25).
  • Burritos: bean ($7.49), regular ($13.49), breakfast burrito with chorizo and eggs ($13.99), super ($15.49), jumbo ($16.49), shrimp or fish ($19.49), and the turbo with both fish and shrimp ($19.49).
  • Quesadillas: regular ($5.25), super ($14.49), jumbo ($14.99), and three quesabirrias ($17.99).
  • Vegetarian: soft tacos ($7.99), tostada ($9.99), quesadilla ($9.99), burrito ($12.99), nachos ($12.99), taco salad ($12.99), and a full vegetarian plate ($13.99).
  • Nachos: regular ($9.99), super with meat ($15.99).
  • Plates: enchiladas ($13.99), taco plate ($13.99), chile relleno ($14.99), an enchilada-and-taco or enchilada-and-chile-relleno combination ($16.49), the two-chile relleno plate ($20.99), three-enchilada plate ($21.99), platos especiales ($21.99), beef or chicken fajitas ($21.99), and fajitas mixtas with steak, chicken, and shrimp ($24.99).
  • Seafood and specialties: meat taco salad ($15.99), tostadas ($14.99), carne en su jugo ($18.99), shrimp cocktail ($19.99), shrimp plate ($22.99), shrimp fajitas ($22.99), and octopus ($20.99).
  • Sides: chips and salsa ($2.99), guacamole ($7.99), rice or beans ($4.49), and the usual add-ons.
  • Breakfast burritos: eggs and potatoes with chorizo, ham, or bacon ($14.99).
  • Drinks: canned and bottled sodas and aguas.

The meat choice runs deep on anything that takes one: carne asada, carnitas, lengua, pollo asado, tripas, pastor, chorizo, buche, and chile verde.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Taqueria Los Gallos have a website?

No. There's no first-party site, which is why the menu above is here. Call 831-217-5000 to check the day's specials.

Can I get Los Gallos delivered?

Yes, through Uber Eats. It's one of two Boulder Creek restaurants on any delivery app. See what food delivery works in Boulder Creek.

Is this the same as the Los Gallos in Scotts Valley?

Same owners, two locations. If you're ordering to a Boulder Creek address, the Uber Eats listing is the Boulder Creek kitchen.

Where is it exactly?

13070 Central Avenue, downtown Boulder Creek, on the main block. Phone 831-217-5000.

Is it sit-down or takeout?

It's a sit-down taqueria with a dining room. Call ahead about takeout.

Last reviewed August 6, 2026. Hours and menu prices change; call 831-217-5000 to confirm.

river-dogs-boulder-creek.title: River Dogs of Boulder Creek: The Hot Dog Stand Behind Joe's Bar
river-dogs-boulder-creek.html:
River Dogs is behind Joe's Bar. Not next to it, not visible from Highway 9: you walk down the side, past Scarborough's, and there's a hot dog cart, a fire pit, some seating, and a small stage in what the owners describe as an area that "has evolved from a storage unit" into somewhere people sit. The stand's own site gives the address as 123 Forest Street and says they are "unofficially" there, and the word fits.

Who runs it

Chris, Kim, and Paul have owned River Dogs since 2019, and they live less than a mile from the cart. This is a neighborhood stand run by neighbors, open when the weather cooperates and closed when it does not.

What they serve

Chicago dogs are the house specialty, built on Vienna Beef and served on steamed poppyseed buns, with homemade garlic aioli and Guinness mustard among the toppings. Order the BigFoot if you want all of them. The board runs:

  • Vienna Beef hot dog, 100 percent beef, straight from Chicago.
  • The Chicago Dog: yellow mustard, atomic relish, onions, a kosher pickle spear, two tomato slices, sport peppers, and a dash of celery salt. It can be built on any other meat or veggie dog for an upgrade.
  • Chili cheese dog, and they will melt the cheese if you ask.
  • Polish or hot Polish, a skinless quarter-pound all-beef sausage with some smoke on it.
  • Bacon dog, the original dog with a smoky slice of bacon; a slice goes on any dog for a small charge.
  • Veggie dogs, made with Field Roast Italian sausages; allow 10 to 15 minutes.
  • The Doggie Dog: a Vienna Beef frank, sliced, no bun, for the dog you brought with you.

The sausage side of the board is seasonal, made locally at Ronnie's Meat Market and cooked to order: a jalapeno cucumber pork sausage built on the Hella Hot hot sauce of the same name, the MegaShred (their featured pork sausage, made with MegaShred hot sauce, exclusive to the stand), a bacon cheddar explosion chicken dog, and a hot Italian. Ask at the cart which are on.

Vegetarians, the veggie dog is a real one and it's great, with the full range of toppings. One heads-up: it adds about ten extra minutes, because they pull it aside and steam it separately just for you, which is the kind of care that makes the wait fine.

Two things are worth knowing before you bring a group. The veggie dogs are a real option and not an afterthought. And there are gluten-free steamed buns, baked by Rotella's, which hold up rather than crumbling.

Your dog is welcome, though not behind the cart, and the stand asks that it be social. There's a fire pit for cold days. No outside food or drink.

Hours, weather, and the stage

There's no roof over any of it, so the schedule bends to the weather. Its posted winter hours run Tuesday through Thursday 11:30 to 3 and Friday through Sunday 11:30 to 5, and it closes for bad weather or special events. Check before you walk down there in January.

The small stage takes acoustic and family-friendly performers, and the owners are open about looking for more of them. They also cater, including job sites, with about a week's notice, and they will arrange orders of $25 or more outside business hours by phone.

River Dogs is also the one restaurant inside Boulder Creek that shows up on DoorDash.

Hours and menu items change, and this one changes with the weather. Check River Dogs' own site or call 831-400-7025 before counting on it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do they cater?

Yes. River Dogs caters events and job sites, and asks for at least a week's notice. Call 831-400-7025 or email riverdogsofbc@gmail.com.

Where exactly is it?

123 Forest Street, behind Joe's Bar and Scarborough's Home and Garden, off Highway 9 in downtown Boulder Creek. You reach it on foot from the main block.

Is there anything for vegetarians?

Yes. Veggie dogs made with Field Roast Italian sausages are on the standing menu, and gluten-free buns are available.

Can I get River Dogs delivered?

Yes. It's on DoorDash, and it's the only Boulder Creek restaurant that is. See what food delivery works in Boulder Creek.

Do they close in bad weather?

Yes. The stand has no roof, so it closes for inclement weather and for special events. Call 831-400-7025 if the day looks marginal.

Last reviewed August 12, 2026. Details follow the stand's own site. The schedule posted there's labeled winter hours, so call before a summer visit.

el-rey-leon-boulder-creek.title: El Rey Leon: The Mexican Food Truck Parked on Central Avenue
el-rey-leon-boulder-creek.html:
El Rey Leon is a food truck with a home. It sets up at 12890 Central Avenue in Boulder Creek on set days each week, with outdoor seating on the lot and a following that knows the schedule.

What it is, and how it runs

Counter service, outside seating, Mexican food. You order at the truck, and you eat at a table on the lot rather than in a dining room. In summer that's most of the appeal. In a February downpour it's the reason Taqueria Los Gallos, a sit-down taqueria on the same street, is the other half of the town's Mexican answer.

I've said elsewhere on this site that I could eat Mexican food every day of the week, and between this truck and Los Gallos, some weeks I nearly manage it. The order in our house splits down the middle. My partner swears by the quesabirria, which comes as three and is somehow never quite enough food, so he always has me add a fourth to round out the order. I'm the vegetarian, and the veggie burrito is the traditional kind, no rice filler, just the beans and the goodies, the way it should be.

The kitchen runs the same hours six days a week: 11 to 3, then a break, then 4 to 7, Monday through Saturday. It's closed Sunday.

One thing worth knowing before you order: call about allergies rather than relying on any posted description.

Ordering, and the menu

Order at the truck or call 831-282-7792. The site's online ordering is currently unavailable, so don't count on placing a pickup or delivery order through the page.

Prices are from August 2026 and will drift; the board at the truck is current.

  • Tacos: tacos ($5.15), Baja fish taco ($7.25), shrimp taco ($7.25), and a taco combo ($17.21).
  • Birria: tacos de birria ($6.20), quesabirria ($7.25), tortabirria ($12.49), quesadilla de birria ($12.49), burrito de birria ($13.55), and the pizzabirria or ramenbirria ($18.80).
  • Burritos: bean and cheese ($9.35), bean, rice, and cheese ($10.40), regular ($12.50), burrito bowl ($13.55), veggie ($13.55), super ($14.60), California ($15.65), and Baja fish or shrimp versions regular ($13.55) or super ($16.70).
  • Quesadillas: regular ($11.45), super ($13.55).
  • Nachos: regular ($14.60), super ($17.75), asada fries ($18.80).
  • Tortas: quesitorta ($12.50), pambazo ($14.60).
  • Burgers: cheeseburger ($10.40), burger combo ($16.70).
  • Extras: salsa or sour cream ($2.53), cheese ($3.05), pico de gallo ($4.10), guacamole ($5.15), chips and salsa ($7.25).

El Rey Leon is one of the few kitchens in Boulder Creek that posts Monday hours at all, which matters in a town where most of the dining rooms close Monday and Tuesday. If you're looking for dinner at the start of the week, this and the markets are the short list.

Hours, menu items, and prices change. Check El Rey Leon's own page or call 831-282-7792 for anything time-sensitive.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is El Rey Leon a truck or a restaurant?

It's a food truck at 12890 Central Avenue with outdoor seating and counter service, there on set days each week.

What are the hours?

Monday through Saturday, 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. and again 4:00 to 7:00 p.m. Closed Sunday.

Can I order ahead?

By phone at 831-282-7792, or order at the truck. Online ordering is currently unavailable.

Is it open on Monday?

Yes, by its posted schedule, which makes it one of the few kitchens in town that is. Scopazzi's, the Red Pearl, and Tae's Edo are all closed Monday.

Where is it exactly?

12890 Central Avenue, downtown Boulder Creek. Phone 831-282-7792.

taes-edo-sushi-boulder-creek.title: Tae's Edo Sushi Bar: The Sushi Restaurant in Boulder Creek
taes-edo-sushi-boulder-creek.html:
Tae's Edo Sushi is the sushi restaurant in Boulder Creek, and for most of the San Lorenzo Valley it's the sushi restaurant full stop. It's at 13271 Highway 9, downtown, and it serves Japanese food six days a week.

When it is open

The schedule is the useful part, because Tae's Edo doesn't run a continuous kitchen. Dinner is 4 to 8, Tuesday through Thursday and Sunday. Friday and Saturday add a lunch window from noon to 3 before the same 4 to 8 dinner. It's closed Monday.

The lunch service is the newer half. The restaurant still leads its own site with a banner announcing it, which is worth knowing if you last checked their hours a while ago.

An 8 p.m. close is early, and normal for this town. The Red Pearl serves later, to 9, and Taqueria Los Gallos runs to 8:45 on weeknights; past that, the kitchens are dark.

What to expect

The restaurant describes its own room as having a "cozy and elegant ambiance," and it's an independent dining room rather than a chain or a counter.

In our house this is the birthday dinner spot: great food across the table and friendly service. One note for plant-based eaters: there aren't many vegetarian options yet; here's hoping the menu grows that direction.

The menu

The full menu lives on the restaurant's own site, which stays current; here is the shape of it, with prices as of August 2026.

The signature rolls are the reason to cross the room: seventeen house rolls, several named for home, including the Boulder Creek ($16), the Highway 9 ($15), the Route 35 ($15), and the Santa Cruz ($18), alongside the Edo Philli ($15), Evergreen ($13), Fire Cracker ($17), FX Spider ($17), Golden CA ($15), Hail Storm ($15), Hot Night ($15), Jumbo ($17), Kapa Fantasy ($16), Mango Bueno ($15), Red Dragon ($17), Roxy ($17), and Yami Yami ($18).

The rest of the board:

  • Maki, cut or hand-rolled ($8 to $12): the classics, from avocado, tuna, salmon, and California rolls up through shrimp tempura, unagi, salmon skin, futo maki, and the spicy tuna, salmon, hamachi, and scallop rolls, plus a Philli roll with salmon, cream cheese, and avocado.
  • Sushi and nigiri ($7 to $18): maguro, sake, hamachi, albacore, ebi, tako, unagi, hotate, hokkigai, kani, inari, tamago, tobiko, and uni at the top of the range.
  • Sashimi: four-piece plates ($14 to $17), a nine-piece assortment ($27), and a sixteen-piece spread ($48).
  • Appetizers ($7 to $19): edamame plain or spicy garlic, gyoza, shrimp tempura, baked mussels, spicy tuna on crispy rice, jalapeno poppers they call the T-Bomb, a tofu plate, and Tommy's Cajun tuna.
  • Salads ($8 to $18): Edo salad, seaweed salad, poki salad, and a Japanese ceviche of assorted sashimi in the house dressing.
  • Specials: chirashi and Korean chirashi ($32), una-don ($32), and the big sashimi platters.
  • Bento: a three-item dinner bento box ($29).

There is sake on the list, hot and cold, from house hot sake ($5) through junmai, nigori, and sparkling bottles, with Kirin and Sapporo and wine by the glass alongside.

Hours and menu items change. Check Tae's Edo Sushi's own page or call 831-338-2099 before you count on anything time-sensitive.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Tae's Edo open for lunch?

Friday and Saturday only, from noon to 3 p.m. Every other day it's dinner service, 4 to 8 p.m.

Is it open on Monday?

No. It's closed Mondays, as are Scopazzi's and the Red Pearl. Monday is the quiet night in Boulder Creek.

Can I order takeout?

Call 831-338-2099. Online ordering is currently disabled, and it's not on the delivery apps, so plan on phoning in a pickup or eating in.

Is there other sushi in the San Lorenzo Valley?

Not in our listings. Tae's Edo is the only sushi bar in the food and drink directory for Boulder Creek or the valley around it.

Where is it exactly?

13271 Highway 9, downtown Boulder Creek, on the main stretch. Phone 831-338-2099.
