bakeries-boulder-creek.title: Bakeries in Boulder Creek: Four Bakers, Four Ways to Buy
bakeries-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek has four bakeries, and not one of them keeps a walk-in storefront of its own. Each of the four has settled on a different way of getting baked goods to you, and between them the town has fresh local baking most days of the week. One sells from a farmstand on weekends. One loads up for the farmers market. One bakes to order from a licensed home kitchen. One is the established cake bakery working out of the back kitchen at a downtown cafe. Here's how you buy from each.

Doughlicious Farmstand: preorder, or catch the weekend stand

The simplest model of the four: bake at home, sell to the neighbors. Doughlicious is run by a baker named Liz from a home on the north side of Boulder Creek, and it works two ways: a weekly order form goes up on its Facebook page for preorders, and the stand itself has been running weekend days, lately Saturday and Sunday with the occasional Friday; her social pages carry each week's days. The stand runs on the honor system, cash or Venmo, and there's a guest book to sign so she knows you came by. The lineup runs to sourdough loaves in a handful of flavors (pesto parmesan, jalapeno cheddar, and roasted garlic and artichoke among them, $6 to $8 a loaf at this writing, sliced on request), plus cinnamon rolls, banana bread, a rotating cast of cookies and sweet treats, farm fresh eggs, and sometimes bagels. A word from experience on the bagels: they are my favorite thing on that table, and they always sell out, so preorder or come early. Questions go to doughliciousbyliz@gmail.com. Because it operates from a home, we don't publish the address; the Facebook page is the front door.

Wildstone Bakery: catch the market stall

Wildstone is the closest thing Boulder Creek has to a dedicated bread bakery, and its model is the market circuit. The bakery is based in town, but the naturally fermented loaves, sourdough bagels, pastries, and seasonal tarts go out to farmers market stalls rather than a shop counter. Its published schedule currently lists the Downtown Santa Cruz Farmers Market on Wednesdays from 12:30 to 5 p.m., and the Ben Lomond Village Market on Mill Street on first Saturdays, June through October, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. The loaves come with names like Raisin Hell and Olive Another Day alongside plain sourdough and ciabatta, and you can call 831-252-0706 or email info@wildstonebakery.com to ask about ordering ahead. It isn't a regular at Boulder Creek's own Thursday market at Junction Park, so plan on Santa Cruz or Ben Lomond for the stall.

Butter Late Than Never: order ahead

Butter Late Than Never Baking Co. skips the stall and the stand entirely. It's a licensed cottage bakery working from a Boulder Creek home kitchen, and everything moves by order: an online shop at butterlatethannever.com for the standing lineup, email for custom requests, and local delivery to get it to you. The lineup leans sweet and playful, with fresh-baked cookies in ice-cream-inspired flavors like Orange Creamsicle and Root Beer Float, plus s'mores cookies, brownies, mini donuts, and cookie cakes. Custom orders go to butterlatethanneverbakingco@gmail.com, and the phone is 510-390-5548. Under California's cottage food rules it can distribute within the state only, which makes it the one Boulder Creek bakery that can send a box to a friend in Sacramento. There's no storefront and no published address, by design.

Dessert First Bakery: order through the counter at Jenna Sue's

Dessert First is the established one, and its business is custom and wholesale baking, specializing in wedding and celebration cakes and desserts made with all-natural ingredients, no preservatives or additives. It has no storefront of its own: it operates out of the back kitchen at Jenna Sue's Cafe, at 13090 Highway 9, Suite 2, and the cafe's counter and phone line are how you reach it. Call 831-338-7008 (the same line as the cafe) or start at dessertfirstbakery.com. This isn't a walk-in bakery with a case to browse; it's an order-ahead operation, so come with a date in hand, especially for a wedding, and ask about delivery for large orders when you book.

Four models, one small town

Towns several times Boulder Creek's size support one bakery or none. Boulder Creek supports four because none of them is carrying the fixed costs of a shop. The farmstand bakes to a weekly preorder list. The market stall goes where the customers already are. The cottage kitchen bakes only what's ordered. The established bakery works out of a cafe's back kitchen and puts the overhead into the cakes. Four different answers to the same problem, and the result is a town where fresh local baking is available most of the week, once you know which form, stall, inbox, or counter to go to.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a walk-in bakery in Boulder Creek?

No. All four bakeries work by preorder, market stall, or custom order rather than a shop counter. For fresh-baked goods without ordering ahead, Jenna Sue's Cafe bakes on site, in the same kitchen Dessert First works from.

Where can I buy sourdough in Boulder Creek?

Through Doughlicious's weekly preorder form or its weekend stand days, or from Wildstone at its farmers market stalls. Our sourdough guide covers the full picture, including a Ben Lomond option.

Who makes custom cakes near Boulder Creek?

Dessert First Bakery takes custom wedding and celebration cake orders, and Butter Late Than Never takes custom orders for cookies, brownies, and cookie cakes. For the full wedding picture, see our wedding venues and vendors guide.

Do any Boulder Creek bakeries deliver?

Butter Late Than Never delivers locally and can ship within California. Dessert First handles delivery on large orders; ask when you order. The other two are pickup operations.

fitness-boulder-creek.title: Fitness and Movement in Boulder Creek: Where to Work Out in Town
fitness-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek doesn't have a gym, and most weeks that matters less than you'd expect. What the town does have is two real studios within a block of downtown, a karate school on the highway, a rec district that runs group classes, and the kind of outdoor terrain that people in flatter places drive hours to reach. Here's the map of where to move in town, and what still means a trip down Highway 9.

Hot yoga and breathwork: Mountain Sangha

The studio at 12788 Highway 9, Suite 1, is Boulder Creek's heated room, a short walk north of downtown with weekday classes starting at 6 a.m. The yoga side runs from hot flow to gentle, yin, and restorative; the strength side is mat-based Hot Pilates, HIIT, and sculpt classes. Then there's the part you'd otherwise drive down the valley for: breathwork sessions, sound baths, and a women's circle, plus private sessions and space rental. Founder Shanon Farney opened the studio after a 20-year corporate career and teaches alongside a deep local roster. Space is limited and booking runs online, so reserve before you drive over. Our full Mountain Sangha guide covers the schedule, the teachers, and current pricing.

Classical Pilates: Treetop Pilates & Wellness

A block away at 125 Forest Street, Treetop Pilates is the studio with the actual apparatus in it: reformer, tower, Cadillac, chair, barrels, and mats. Mat classes cap at eight people, tower classes at three, and machine work is booked as a private, duet, or trio, so nobody disappears into the back row. The studio recommends starting one-on-one before joining a group. Tammy Ogletree founded the studio in 2017 and teaches classical Pilates built around what a particular body can do. There's no timetable published online, so the phone is the way in: 831-419-0202 or 831-421-1224. The full Treetop Pilates guide has formats, intro offers, and prices.

The rest of the in-town list

Lone Wolf Kenpo Academy teaches karate right downtown at 13089 Highway 9, for a range of ages. And the Boulder Creek Recreation and Park District runs the closest thing in town to a group-class schedule, from Jazzercise to free body sculpting to pickleball, plus a summer pool at Bear Creek. The lineup rotates by season, so we keep the details in our gyms and fitness guide and the district keeps the current schedule.

The gym question

Here's the boundary: there's no full gym in Boulder Creek. You can walk to a reformer and a heated yoga room, but not to a squat rack. The nearest weight rooms are down Highway 9, and two cover most needs. Toadal Fitness Scotts Valley, at 269 Mount Hermon Road, is the family-oriented full-service club, with group classes and a supervised kids area for ages 3 months to 12 years, open weekdays 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. and weekends 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Enterprise Sports Club, at 100 Enterprise Way, Suite G100, is the biggest facility in reach, a 26,000-square-foot athletic club with an outdoor pool, spa, sauna, and tennis, pickleball, and basketball courts, open to the public since 2020. Our gyms comparison covers both in detail, plus the closer strength-and-conditioning option in Felton.

The free option: go outside

Boulder Creek's real fitness asset doesn't take a membership. Garrahan Park has a walking track and a soccer field, open sunrise to sunset. In summer, the river beach at Junction Park is the town's swimming hole, unguarded and swim at your own risk, so read the safety basics first. And nine miles up Highway 236 sits Big Basin, open for limited day use from 8 a.m. to sunset as it recovers from the 2020 fire, with the easy 0.6-mile Redwood Loop as the classic first walk. Check what's currently open before you go, then use the day trip guide to plan it right, parking reservation included. A hill town is a stair machine with better views.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a gym in Boulder Creek?

No full gym, but more than nothing: Mountain Sangha for hot yoga and movement, Treetop Pilates for classical machine work, Lone Wolf Kenpo for karate, and rec district classes. For a weight room, see our gyms comparison.

Where can I take a yoga class in town?

Mountain Sangha at 12788 Highway 9, Suite 1. Classes run from early morning on weekdays, space is limited, and booking is online through the studio's site.

Do I need experience to start Pilates at Treetop?

No. The studio recommends starting one-on-one before joining group classes, and there's an introductory assessment for exactly that. Call 831-419-0202 to set it up.

What's the closest place to hike?

Big Basin's main entrance is about 9 miles up Highway 236, open for limited day use while it recovers. Confirm what's open on the official park page the morning you go.

churches-boulder-creek.title: Churches and Congregations in Boulder Creek, Plus the Buildings That Came First
churches-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek keeps three active congregations, one Catholic, one United Methodist, and one Baptist, and all three sit within a few blocks of downtown. That's the practical half of this page: who meets where, and when. The other half is history, because two of the town's church buildings are on file with the county as historic resources, and one of them is the oldest church building still standing in Boulder Creek. It just isn't a church anymore.

One ground rule before the list: this page describes, it doesn't endorse. Inclusion isn't a recommendation of any congregation or tradition, and the service times below shift more often than business hours do. Confirm before visiting, especially around holidays.

St. Michael's Catholic Church

  • Address: 13005 Pine Street, Boulder Creek
  • Phone: 831-338-6112
  • Website: stmichaelschurchbc.org
  • Mass: Sunday 10 a.m.; Wednesday 9:30 a.m.; call to confirm

The town's Catholic parish sits on Pine Street a couple of blocks off the main drag, part of the Diocese of Monterey. As of this writing the parish publishes a Sunday 10 a.m. Mass and a Wednesday morning Mass at 9:30, with Holy Day schedules announced separately; the site currently notes no Saturday vigil, though older listings around the web still show one, which is exactly why you call first. The parish office keeps short hours, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday mornings from 9 to 11. Catholic roots in town run deep: a first Catholic church went up around 1900 and was replaced mid-century by a larger building.

Boulder Creek United Methodist Church

  • Address: 12855 Boulder Street, Boulder Creek
  • Phone: 831-338-6232
  • Website: bcumc.com
  • Worship: Sunday 10 a.m., in person and on Zoom; confirm before visiting

The Methodist congregation worships in the 1908 landmark at Boulder and Mountain Streets (more on the building below) and belongs to the El Camino Real District of the United Methodist Church's California-Nevada Conference. The church publishes a Sunday 10 a.m. service, offered both in the sanctuary and over Zoom, plus a Thursday morning Bible study online. It also functions as one of the town's quiet community buildings: it hosts Girl Scout and Boy Scout troops, Alcoholics Anonymous groups, and rehearsal and performance space for the Concerto Strings orchestra.

Boulder Creek Community Church

  • Address: 12465 Highway 9, Boulder Creek
  • Phone: 831-338-3700
  • Website: bccchurch.org
  • Services: Sunday 9 a.m. and 10:45 a.m.; confirm before visiting

At the south end of town on Highway 9, Boulder Creek Community Church is a Southern Baptist congregation that runs two Sunday services, at 9 and 10:45 a.m., and livestreams on YouTube for anyone up a long driveway on a stormy morning. The church runs a youth ministry and keeps a prayer text line at 831-338-PRAY.

The two historic church buildings

Boulder Creek's church history is longer and rougher than its current roster suggests, and the county's historic-resource files tell most of the story.

The oldest church building still standing in town is the little Gothic Revival chapel at 12547 Highway 9, built in 1906 as Grace Episcopal Church. A lay reader named Arthur Darwall and his son built it from local redwood, pointed-arch windows and all, in what was then the separate town of Lorenzo. The Episcopal congregation consolidated with Ben Lomond's around 1915, the Christian Science Society bought the building in 1923, and in 1995 it passed to the Boulder Creek Historical Society. Today it houses the San Lorenzo Valley Museum, so you can walk through it on an ordinary afternoon, original redwood walls, scissor trusses, and one surviving pew included.

The Methodist building at 12855 Boulder Street is the survivor of a harder run. Methodist class meetings in the valley date to about 1865, and the congregation's first church went up in Lorenzo in the mid-1870s, built by J.W. Peery. It burned in 1885, was rebuilt the same year, and burned again in 1907, a fire rumored at the time (never proven) to be arson by the saloon element the congregation kept preaching against. The present Carpenter Gothic building, with its square tower and four shingled corner turrets, went up in 1908, built again by Peery with $500 from the Methodist Home Mission Board and local donations. It has stood on the same corner ever since, with a school wing added in 1949. The whole saga, fires included, fits the pattern in our town history timeline.

What this page doesn't cover

Mountain Sangha, despite the name, isn't a congregation; it's a yoga and movement studio on Highway 9, covered in its own article. And some traditions that once had a house of worship in town no longer do: there's been no Episcopal congregation here since the 1915 consolidation, and the Presbyterian church lost to fire in 1908 was never replaced in town. For denominations without a Boulder Creek presence, the nearest options are down the valley in Ben Lomond, Felton, and Scotts Valley. Separately, Valley Churches United Missions in Ben Lomond, a valley charity with church roots, runs the area's food pantry and appears in our directory.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many churches does Boulder Creek have?

Three active congregations: St. Michael's Catholic Church on Pine Street, Boulder Creek United Methodist Church on Boulder Street, and Boulder Creek Community Church (Baptist) on Highway 9.

What's the oldest church building in Boulder Creek?

The 1906 Grace Episcopal Church building at 12547 Highway 9, per its county historic-resource file. It's no longer a church; it houses the San Lorenzo Valley Museum, and it's open to visitors.

Is there a Catholic Mass in Boulder Creek?

Yes. St. Michael's publishes a Sunday 10 a.m. Mass and a Wednesday 9:30 a.m. Mass. Schedules shift, so call 831-338-6112 before you go.

Which churches offer online services?

Boulder Creek United Methodist publishes a Zoom option for its Sunday service, and Boulder Creek Community Church livestreams on YouTube. Confirm links on each church's own site.

Is this page recommending a church?

No. It lists what exists, even-handedly, and takes no position on any congregation or tradition. Visit, ask questions, and decide for yourself.

boulder-creek-veterinary-clinic.title: Boulder Creek Veterinary Clinic: The Vet on Highway 9
boulder-creek-veterinary-clinic.html:
Boulder Creek's veterinary clinic sits right on the main drag at 12870 Highway 9. Boulder Creek Veterinary Clinic is a full-service companion-animal practice, which in plain terms means most of what your pet needs across its life happens in one building: checkups, vaccines, dental work, surgery, and urgent care when something goes wrong.

That matters more here than it would over the hill. The nearest alternative in the town directory is down the valley in Felton, so having exams, X-rays, and an in-house lab a few minutes from home saves mountain families a winding drive with a sick animal in the back seat.

What the clinic handles

The clinic's published services cover the routine and the not-so-routine:

  • Wellness care: new puppy and kitten visits, annual physical exams, vaccines, and deworming
  • Dental: teeth cleaning and dental services, including dental X-rays
  • Surgery: spay and neuter, plus general surgical care
  • Diagnostics: an in-house laboratory, radiology, and ultrasound
  • Treatment: heartworm disease treatment and laser therapy
  • Grooming: therapeutic bathing and grooming services
  • Extras: exotic pet care, pet boarding, and travel certificates for pets crossing borders

The exotics line is worth underlining. Plenty of clinics stop at dogs and cats, so if your household includes something with feathers or scales, this is one of the closer places that will see it. Call first to confirm they treat your particular animal.

The pet shop inside

The clinic doubles as the town's small pet shop. Inside the same building there's a retail corner with food, treats, toys, and supplies, which means a vet visit and the errand for a bag of food can be one stop instead of a drive down the valley. Worth knowing even when nobody's sick.

Emergencies

The clinic describes itself as fully staffed and equipped for emergency veterinary services. If your pet is in trouble during open hours, the clinic's own advice is simple: stop reading and call, at 831-338-7205. For anything after hours, call anyway; the recording or the staff can point you to the right place. Confirm the after-hours plan before you need it, because that's not a detail to figure out at midnight.

Booking and paperwork

Appointments run through the PetDesk mobile app, which the clinic uses for scheduling and pet-health records, or by phone. New clients can knock out the paperwork ahead of time; the clinic posts its new-client form, medical release, and other forms online. It also links to two online pharmacies (Covetrus and VetsFirstChoice) for refills shipped to your door.

No prices are published, so call for estimates before a big procedure.

Hours and where it is

The clinic is at 12870 Highway 9 in downtown Boulder Creek, phone 831-338-7205. Posted hours:

  • Monday and Wednesday: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.
  • Tuesday, Thursday, Friday: 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
  • Saturday: 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Sunday: closed

The two evening nights and Saturday hours are a real convenience if you work over the hill. Hours change, so confirm before you drive over.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is Boulder Creek Veterinary Clinic?

12870 Highway 9, Boulder Creek, CA 95006, on the main road through downtown. Phone 831-338-7205.

Do they see exotic pets?

Yes, exotic pet care is on the clinic's published services list. Call ahead to confirm they treat your specific animal.

Can they handle emergencies?

The clinic says it's fully staffed and equipped for emergency veterinary services during open hours. Call 831-338-7205 first so they can prepare for your arrival.

How do I book an appointment?

Through the PetDesk mobile app or by phone. New-client forms are posted on the clinic's website so you can fill them out before your first visit.

Do they do dental work?

Yes, teeth cleaning and dental services including dental X-rays are on the services list.

Is there boarding?

Pet boarding appears on the clinic's published services. Call to confirm availability and which animals they board.

childcare-boulder-creek.title: Childcare in Boulder Creek: Start Here
childcare-boulder-creek.html:
Childcare is the quiet math problem behind every working family on the mountain, and the answer depends almost entirely on your child's age. Boulder Creek has real options for a town this size, but they're small, phone-based, and specific about the ages they take. So instead of one long list, we've split the map by band: pick your kid's age, and start there.

Ground rules across all of these: inclusion isn't endorsement, and for home-based daycares we print the community and phone number only, never a home address; the call is how you arrange a visit anyway.

Babies and toddlers (0 to about 2)

The scarcest band, and the one to start on earliest. In town, Little People's School holds a state infant-center license and Adina's Daycare has taken infants in its licensed family child care home since 1991, with more options in Ben Lomond. Who takes babies, and how the waitlists really work, is in our infant care guide.

Preschool age (about 2 to TK)

The widest band. Seeds of Knowledge is the town's licensed full-day preschool, Busy Bees runs play-based programs in Boulder Creek (mornings, Monday to Thursday) and Ben Lomond (a full 8-to-5 day), and the state-subsidized preschool option sits ten minutes south. The full list, including partial-day rec programs and the TK boundary, is in our preschools guide.

School-age kids

Once school covers the middle of the day, you're solving for the edges: before the bell, after it, early-out Wednesdays, and summer. The YMCA's on-campus care at Boulder Creek Elementary and the rec district's walk-down enrichment classes carry most of it; the details are in our after-school care guide.

For school itself, TK through 12th grade, our SLV schools guide covers enrollment, campuses, and transfers, and the valley-wide childcare explainer breaks down how the different license types work.

Two shortcuts that apply at every age

The county's Child Development Resource Center (831-466-5820, weekdays 8 to 5) gives free referrals to licensed programs with current openings anywhere in the county, including subsidized options. It's the fastest way past cold-calling.

And before you enroll anywhere, look the provider up on the state's Community Care Licensing search, which shows current license status for every licensed home and center in California.

Beyond the licensed programs, plenty of valley families rely on word-of-mouth and app-based sitters and nanny shares, and drop-in playgroups, story times, and kids' classes fill the gaps between care; those land on our events page when they're scheduled.

Frequently Asked Questions

What childcare exists in Boulder Creek itself?

Two licensed infant and toddler providers, a licensed full-day preschool, a licensed family child care home for preschool age, license-exempt rec programs, and YMCA before- and after-school care at the elementary school. Each age-band guide above has contacts and details.

Where do families go when in-town options are full?

Ben Lomond, mostly: a licensed child care center, a home daycare, and the Highlands Park Early Education Center, which runs the state preschool program for income-eligible families. Felton and Scotts Valley add more; the referral line at 831-466-5820 can search countywide.

How far ahead should I plan?

The younger the child, the longer the lead. Infant lists move slowest, preschool spots turn over yearly, and after-school programs fill at the start of each session. Calling early and joining several lists is normal here.

infant-care-boulder-creek.title: Infant Care in and Around Boulder Creek: Who Takes Babies
infant-care-boulder-creek.html:
This article is the reason Boulder Creek Local exists. When our baby arrived and my return to a demanding job started counting down, I went looking for infant care and found almost nothing to look at. The valley's providers are real, and some of them are wonderful, but most have no website and no active social media, so as far as a search engine is concerned they barely exist. I finally secured a spot the old mountain way: through word of mouth, one recommendation at a time, while the clock ran.

Somewhere between those conversations and the first day of care, it clicked that half this valley solves its problems this way, and that somebody should start writing the answers down. That's how this site began. So if you're reading this late at night with a due date approaching and a return-to-work date after that, this page is the one I needed and couldn't find. Ground rules: inclusion isn't endorsement, and for home-based care we print the community and phone only, never a home address; the call is how you arrange a visit anyway.

In town: two licensed options

Little People's School (13155 Oak Street, 831-566-4236) is the anchor for this age band. A longtime in-town program, it now focuses on infants and toddlers, roughly babies up to age three, and holds a state infant-center license, the license type specifically for the under-two crowd. Ages served have shifted over the years, so confirm the current range and openings when you call.

Adina's Daycare (831-338-3873) is a licensed family child care home that's operated in Boulder Creek since 1991, taking infants through preschool age on weekdays. A home setting means small, mixed-age groups, and for a baby it also means your toddler can eventually stay in the same place. It's home-based, so call to arrange a visit.

That's the in-town list: two providers, both reached by phone.

Down the valley

The Highlands Park Early Education Center (8500 Highway 9, Ben Lomond, 831-400-1170), a Community Bridges program, offers licensed infant, toddler, and preschool care, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. It also runs the California State Preschool Program for income-eligible families, so if cost is the constraint, this is the first call.

Osito's Day Care (831-336-8486) is a licensed, home-based, bilingual English and Spanish program in Ben Lomond that starts around 12 months, so it's an option for older babies rather than newborns. Weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.; confirm the starting age when you call.

In Felton, Quail Hollow Montessori (187 Laurel Drive), part of the Little Acorns Montessori family of schools, takes infants from 6 months in a dedicated infant class, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with half-day and extended options; it enrolls by application and waitlist.

Mountain Buddies, a home-based daycare in Ben Lomond, posts openings on its public Facebook page; the owner describes care for babies 3 to 23 months with part-time, full-time, and drop-in options in a very small group. Its license status isn't posted, so run the state lookup below and ask directly before enrolling.

How to land a spot

Infant spots turn over slowest because babies stay for years. Openings appear when a child ages up, not on a semester calendar: call every provider whose range fits, ask to be added to the list, and check back monthly. Parents who start during pregnancy aren't being dramatic; they're being realistic.

Two tools help. The county's Child Development Resource Center (831-466-5820, weekdays 8 to 5) gives free referrals to licensed programs with current openings, including subsidized options. And before enrolling anywhere, look the provider up on the state's Community Care Licensing search to confirm the license is current.

Once your child nears two, the options widen considerably; our preschools guide covers that band, and the childcare overview maps every age.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does anyone in Boulder Creek take babies?

Yes, two licensed providers: Little People's School on Oak Street, which holds a state infant-center license, and Adina's Daycare, a licensed family child care home operating since 1991. Both are weekday programs; call for current openings.

When should I start looking for infant care?

As early as you can, ideally before the baby arrives. Lists move slowly, and being on several at once is normal and expected.

Is there subsidized infant care nearby?

Highlands Park Early Education Center in Ben Lomond offers licensed infant care, and the county referral line at 831-466-5820 can walk you through subsidy programs countywide.

preschools-boulder-creek.title: Preschools in and Around Boulder Creek
preschools-boulder-creek.html:
Somewhere between the second birthday and TK, most Boulder Creek families go looking for a preschool, and this is the band the town covers best: a licensed full-day preschool, a play-based home program, and partial-day options, plus a deeper bench down the valley. Ground rules: inclusion isn't endorsement, and home-based programs get a community and contact path only, never a home address.

In town

Seeds of Knowledge Preschool (16900 Highway 9, 831-251-5711) is Boulder Creek's licensed preschool, open Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m., the town's one full-workday option for this age. The program is hands-on and play-based, with a flexible, individualized curriculum and low teacher-to-student ratios; tours can be scheduled by phone or email.

Busy Bees Playschool, a licensed family child care home founded by Michelle Hamblin Mathews, is the town's newest option: a play-based, child-led program for ages 2 through kindergarten that spends most of its day outdoors. It runs Monday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., and prices by the number of days you take, from one day a week up to four. Reach Michelle at 831-251-0921 or busybeesmichelle@gmail.com; tours are welcome.

Its second location, Busy Bees Playschool Two, is a licensed child care center at 7985 Highway 9 in Ben Lomond for ages 2 to 6, and it runs the longer day, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. That one is reachable at 831-289-3012 or busybeeskimberly@gmail.com. Between them the two sites cover both shapes of the problem: a school-morning program up here, and a full working day down the valley.

For partial-day routine rather than full-day care, Little Explorers Play & Grow, the rec district's preschool-prep program for toddlers and preschoolers, runs Tuesday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., on a school-year calendar; confirm the starting age and rates with the district (831-338-4144). It's license-exempt recreation, not licensed daycare; the full lineup lives in our kids' activities guide.

Down the valley

The Highlands Park Early Education Center (8500 Highway 9, Ben Lomond, 831-400-1170), a Community Bridges program open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., offers licensed preschool care and runs the California State Preschool Program for income-eligible families, the first call if cost is the constraint. Osito's Day Care in Ben Lomond also serves this band; since it starts around 12 months, it's covered in our infant care guide.

The county's Kreative Kids Preschool, a license-exempt recreation program, meets Monday through Thursday mornings at Wilder Hall in Ben Lomond Park for ages 3 to 6.

Felton adds two more. Quail Hollow Montessori (187 Laurel Drive) runs Montessori classes from 18 months through kindergarten, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., with half-day and extended options, enrolling by application and waitlist; its infant class is covered in our infant care guide. The Santa Cruz Forest School runs an outdoor program for ages 3 to 6, Monday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., year-round; its childcare license status isn't posted, so ask if you need licensed care.

Federal school records list Ludlow Preschool, an SLVUSD-operated preschool at 7101 Highway 9 in Felton; call the district (831-336-5194) about eligibility and enrollment.

Preschool or TK?

If your child turns four before September 1, free transitional kindergarten through the school district enters the picture; enrollment is covered in our SLV schools guide, and the valley-wide childcare explainer lays out how the license types differ.

The county's Child Development Resource Center (831-466-5820, weekdays 8 to 5) gives free referrals to licensed programs with openings, including subsidized options, and the state's Community Care Licensing search confirms any provider's license. For other ages, the childcare overview maps the whole landscape.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a full-day preschool in Boulder Creek?

Yes. Seeds of Knowledge Preschool at 16900 Highway 9 runs Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.; call 831-251-5711 for openings and tours.

Is there state-subsidized preschool nearby?

Yes. Highlands Park Early Education Center in Ben Lomond runs the California State Preschool Program for income-eligible families, and the county referral line at 831-466-5820 covers subsidy options countywide.

What's the difference between a preschool and a rec program?

A licensed preschool or family child care home can provide full-day care under state childcare licensing. Recreation programs like Little Explorers and Kreative Kids are license-exempt, partial-day enrichment: good routine, not full-day care.

after-school-care-boulder-creek.title: After-School Care in Boulder Creek: Covering the Edges of the School Day
after-school-care-boulder-creek.html:
School solves childcare from bell to bell and leaves you the edges: the 7 a.m. shift start, the 2:45 pickup, early-out Wednesdays, and the long weeks of summer. Boulder Creek's coverage for those gaps is thin but real, and most of it runs through two doors, the elementary school campus and the rec district.

On campus: YMCA before- and after-school care

The YMCA runs before- and after-school childcare right on the Boulder Creek Elementary campus, operated independently of the school and the district. That on-site part matters: no second dropoff, no mid-afternoon shuttle. The school's site lists 408-914-0608 for information and cost; call for current hours, availability, and registration. Enrollment at the school itself is a separate process, covered in our SLV schools guide.

One calendar note worth planning around: elementary early-out is weekly here. Boulder Creek Elementary releases at 1:15 p.m. on Wednesdays for most of the year, a detail that shapes which coverage you actually need; the schools guide has the current calendar.

TK aftercare in Ben Lomond

If your child is in transitional kindergarten, Busy Bees Playschool Two at 7985 Highway 9 in Ben Lomond runs a TK aftercare program built around the bus: they collect TK children from the bus stop and walk them to the school, the kids bring a lunchbox and water bottle, and there's organized quiet time and play until parent pickup, which runs until 5 p.m. Five days a week is priced as a flat monthly rate. Spots are limited; ask at busybeeskimberly@gmail.com or 831-289-3012.

After the bell: the rec district

The rec district fills afternoons in six-week enrichment sessions that run from the start of school through mid-December: robotics, gym, cooking, and sports, mostly for ages 6 to 11. A walk-down from Boulder Creek Elementary is available for a small add-on fee, meaning staff walk the kids over from campus, the detail that makes a 3 p.m. class workable for a working parent, and one gym session is timed to Wednesday's early-out afternoon. Sessions fill, so register early through the district's forms (rec center: 831-338-4144).

For twelve and up, the district's Friday-evening Hangout downtown is a drop-in, not childcare, but it covers the age nothing else does. The full current lineup, including the library's free school-age programs on West Park Avenue, lives in our kids' activities guide.

Summer and school breaks

The walk-downs and campus care follow the school calendar, so breaks are their own project. For summer, day camps and the valley's overnight camps are mapped in our summer camps guide; registration timing matters more than anything else there, and that guide covers it.

For younger siblings, our infant care and preschools guides cover the pre-K bands, and the childcare overview maps the whole landscape.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there before-school care at Boulder Creek Elementary?

Yes. The YMCA runs before- and after-school care on campus, independently of the district. Call 408-914-0608 for hours, cost, and registration.

What covers early-out Wednesdays?

The YMCA's on-campus care and the rec district's afternoon sessions are the structured options; confirm with each that Wednesday's early release is covered. Boulder Creek Elementary releases at 1:15 p.m. most Wednesdays.

What happens after the rec sessions end in December?

The enrichment sessions run August through mid-December, so winter afternoons lean on the YMCA program, the library's free programs, and basketball season. The kids' activities guide covers the winter options.

pet-boarding-sitting-boulder-creek.title: Pet Boarding and Sitting Near Boulder Creek: Where the Dog Stays
pet-boarding-sitting-boulder-creek.html:
Every trip out of town starts with the same question: where does the dog stay? Boulder Creek has more answers than you'd guess, and they run from a kennel run by your own vet to a sitter who comes up the mountain so your cat never leaves the house. Here's the full list, closest first.

In town: boarding at the vet

Boulder Creek Veterinary Clinic at 12870 Highway 9 lists pet boarding among its published services, and boarding at a veterinary practice has an obvious appeal for an animal with a health condition: it's the one option where the building is also a clinic. The clinic doesn't publish boarding availability or which animals it takes, so call 831-338-7205 before you build a trip around it. That's the only boarding option inside Boulder Creek itself; everything else means at least a short drive.

Down the valley: Felton's two options

Felton Veterinary Hospital at 5996 Highway 9 offers supervised boarding for dogs and cats, with grooming available at the same stop, so a pet can come home from a week away freshly bathed. The hospital posts a boarding admittance form on its site, which tells you they'll want paperwork sorted before drop-off; ask what it requires when you book at 831-335-3466. Office hours are Monday through Friday 8 to 6 and Saturday 8 to 2, which frames your drop-off and pickup windows.

Camp Happy Tails, based in Felton, is the valley's dedicated pet-care business: doggy daycare, boarding, grooming, and in-home pet sitting across the San Lorenzo Valley, and it describes itself as fully insured, licensed, and bonded. The sitting side is the piece nothing else on this page offers. For a cat, a flock of chickens, or a dog that does badly in kennels, a sitter who handles feeding, medication, and company at your own house is often the calmer answer, and it solves the mountain-specific problem of animals that shouldn't travel down Highway 9 twice. Call 831-247-8245.

Down in Santa Cruz: the 24-hour facility

When you want a staffed building around the clock, the nearest facility that publishes it is Bed & Biscuits Groomingdales at 2625 Chanticleer Avenue in Santa Cruz, which boards dogs and cats and says it's staffed 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. It's a full campus: daycare, grooming, and dog training alongside the boarding. Office hours are Monday through Friday 7:30 to 6, Saturday 8 to 2, and two short Sunday windows, with other times by appointment. Call 831-475-1580.

App-based sitters (Rover and similar) also operate in the valley. They're a real category, and plenty of people use them happily, but they're individual arrangements we can't verify the way we verify a business, so we don't list individuals here.

What to ask before you book

The questions are the same everywhere, so ask them once, early:

  • Vaccination records. Boarding facilities generally require proof of vaccination; ask which ones and bring the paperwork. Felton Vet's admittance form is posted online, so you can get ahead of that one.
  • Medications and quirks. If your pet takes medication or has a routine that matters, confirm the provider will handle it and write it down at drop-off.
  • Holiday lead time. Thanksgiving through New Year's books up everywhere. If the trip is planned, book the boarding when you book the flights.
  • A trial run. For a first-time boarder, a single daycare day or one overnight before a long trip tells you more than any phone call.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there dog boarding in Boulder Creek?

Boulder Creek Veterinary Clinic lists boarding among its services; call 831-338-7205 to confirm availability. The nearest confirmed dog and cat boarding is Felton Veterinary Hospital, down Highway 9 at 831-335-3466.

Who does in-home pet sitting in the San Lorenzo Valley?

Camp Happy Tails, a licensed, bonded, and insured Felton-based business, offers pet sitting with feeding, medication, and companionship, plus daycare and boarding. Call 831-247-8245.

Where's the nearest boarding facility staffed overnight?

Bed & Biscuits Groomingdales in Santa Cruz, 2625 Chanticleer Avenue, says it's staffed 24 hours a day, every day. Phone 831-475-1580.

Can my pet get groomed while boarding?

Yes, at two of these: Felton Veterinary Hospital offers grooming alongside boarding, and so does Bed & Biscuits. In town, Bowzer Baths grooms by appointment but doesn't board.

annual-events-boulder-creek.title: Boulder Creek's Year: The Big Annual Events
annual-events-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek runs on a handful of big days that come back every year, in the same order. Pancakes at the firehouse on the Fourth. A barbecue in the apparatus bay in August. A harvest festival when the weather turns. Candy on Highway 9, then Santa lighting the tree downtown. This page is the year at a glance, January through Christmas Eve: what each event is, who runs it, and roughly when it lands. This year's confirmed dates and times are on the events calendar.

Late winter: the BCVFD Crab Feed

The Boulder Creek Volunteer Fire Department's Crab Feed is the first big night of the year: a sit-down dinner of fresh crab, pasta, salad, and bread at the fire station on Central Avenue, served by the volunteers themselves. It's landed in March in recent years, tickets are capped at what the room holds, and it tends to sell out, so plan ahead. Proceeds keep the all-volunteer department equipped.

Late spring: Lumberjack Days, now at Roaring Camp

After its years in Boulder Creek, Lumberjack Days has moved to a larger venue, Roaring Camp down the valley in Felton, and it's worth the trip. The day is built around real logging competitions (axe throwing, chainsaw classes, choker setting, bucking saw, vertical chopping) with a King or Queen of the Woods crowned, plus kids' events, barbecue, beer and cider, and live music. Admission has been free, and Roaring Camp sets the date, so check the events calendar for the current one.

Every Fourth of July: pancakes, the parade, and Junction Park

The Fourth is the town's biggest day. The volunteer firefighters serve a pancake breakfast at the firehouse from early morning toward noon, a fundraiser for medical and rescue equipment. The parade follows Highway 9 through downtown at mid-morning, a tradition the business association says the town has held for generations, and a barbecue with live bands at Junction Park carries the afternoon. Highway 9 closes through downtown while the parade runs, so park once and walk.

An August Saturday: the BCVFD Summer BBQ & Dance

One night every August, the engines roll out onto the apron and the tables go into the apparatus bay for the fire department's biggest fundraiser, the Summer BBQ & Dance. Firefighters cook and serve tri-tip and chicken, bands play on a stage out back until late, and there's a bounce house for the kids. It stays a working fire station the whole night, and the proceeds buy rescue and medical equipment. Later in August, community radio KBCZ 89.3 throws its own party, the KBCZ Music Fest, an afternoon of live bands at Garrahan Park and the station's main fundraiser.

Early fall: the Santa Cruz Mountain Harvest Festival

When the weather turns, downtown gets one more big afternoon. The Harvest Festival fills Junction Park and the Downtown Rec Center with live music, food vendors, local beer and wine, and dozens of area artists and makers. The Recreation and Park District and its foundation run it as a fundraiser for community nonprofits. It's all ages, and it has recently landed on a Saturday in late September. Plan for sun and tight parking.

Halloween: trick-or-treat down Highway 9

Mountain driveways are too long and too dark for door-to-door, so on Halloween evening the town brings the candy to one strip instead. Downtown merchants along Highway 9 hand out candy in the early evening, usually about 5 to 7 p.m., with volunteers helping families cross the highway. The business association and the merchants run it, and adults and dogs come costumed too. Our downtown trick-or-treat guide covers the route, the crossing points, and how the tradition started.

Thanksgiving into December: the tree lighting at the Winter Festival

The holidays center on one moment: Santa arriving to light the town Christmas tree on Forest Street. Around it, the Winter Festival runs a full afternoon, with live music, artisan vendors, a food court, and free activities like a snow-play area and a hay ride, plus ticketed extras like Santa photos. The Boulder Creek Business Association leads it, with the Recreation and Park District and the Odd Fellows as partners, and it's free to walk into. Timing runs late November or early December, varying year to year, so check the events calendar and the BCBA. The holiday events guide has the full picture.

Christmas Eve: the Reindeer Run

The year closes at a run. On Christmas Eve morning, runners, walkers, strollers, and plenty of costumes leave Junction Park for a 5K along Highway 9 and Irwin Way. The Recreation and Park District Foundation puts it on as its own fundraiser; all abilities are welcome, kids 12 and under are free, and registration runs through the run's site, with details on the events calendar too.

And every week and month in between

Two smaller rhythms fill the gaps. First Friday keeps downtown open late on the first Friday of every month, 5 to 8 p.m., with art, vendor tables, and music along the strip. And the farmers market sets up at Junction Park on Thursday afternoons, May through October. Together they're most of the town's regular social calendar, and both are on the events calendar week by week.

Frequently asked questions

When is the Boulder Creek 4th of July parade?

Every Fourth of July. Pancakes at the firehouse in the early morning, the parade down Highway 9 at mid-morning, and the Junction Park barbecue in the afternoon. Confirmed times are on the events calendar.

When is the Boulder Creek tree lighting?

During the Winter Festival on Forest Street downtown, which lands Thanksgiving weekend into early December, set fresh each year. Check the events calendar as the holidays approach.

Who runs the pancake breakfast?

The Boulder Creek Volunteer Fire Department, every Fourth of July morning at the firehouse on Central Avenue. There's a per-plate charge, and the department says the money goes toward medical and rescue equipment.

Where do I find this year's dates?

The events calendar carries current dates, times, and ticket links for everything here. Each event's article covers the rest.

Organizers, times, and formats do shift. If something here has changed, tell us. If you're new in town, the directory will tell you who's behind most of these names.

hiking-boulder-creek.title: Hiking in and Around Boulder Creek: Where the Trails Are
hiking-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek has always been a trailhead town. Big Basin's front door is up the highway, Castle Rock sits on the ridge above, and two more redwood parks are a short drive down the valley. The catch, since the 2020 CZU fire, is that "what's open" changes more often than any guide can promise. Treat this page as a map of options, not a guarantee, and check each park's own page before you drive. Every status below comes from the parks' official pages as of August 7, 2026.

The Miller property: the newest place to walk

The closest new option is Miller Property County Park, a 410-acre open space on Kings Creek Road about three miles north of town, opened to the public by Santa Cruz County Parks in August 2025. It's open sunrise to sunset daily, with nature trails along Kings Creek, a gated dirt parking lot and portable restroom at the entrance, and leashed dogs welcome; fires, alcohol, and motorized vehicles aren't. The county and Santa Cruz Mountains Trail Stewardship are building out a three-mile multi-use trail network through spring 2027, so expect basic facilities and some construction activity. We've got a full writeup coming; for now, expect a quiet, unpolished walk.

Big Basin Redwoods State Park

Big Basin is the big one, nine miles up Highway 236 from downtown, and it's open for limited day use, 8 a.m. to sunset, while it recovers from the CZU fire. Camping remains closed, parking is limited, and a reservation is strongly recommended. Rather than repeat details that shift month to month, start with our guide to what's actually open at Big Basin, then use the day trip guide to plan the outing itself. For the deeper story of the park and the town, read how Big Basin became California's first state park.

Castle Rock State Park

Castle Rock sits at the top of the ridge, up Highway 9 where it meets Skyline Boulevard, and it's a different mountain than the valley floor: higher, drier, with sandstone formations that have made it a rock climbing destination for decades. As of this writing the park's page lists trails and climbing open, day use from 6 a.m. to sunset, and $10 per vehicle at the Kirkwood entrance. Two things to know before you commit: dogs aren't allowed, and the park's own page warns there's no cell reception in or around the park, so download your map and tell someone your plan.

Henry Cowell Redwoods and the Fall Creek Unit

Down the valley near Felton, Henry Cowell Redwoods State Park is the easy win: open sunrise to sunset, $10 per vehicle, a visitor center open daily, and old-growth redwoods close to the parking. It's the flattest, most forgiving redwood walking in the area, which makes it the right call with kids or anyone easing into hiking.

Henry Cowell's Fall Creek Unit, on the far side of Felton, is the opposite personality: day use only, no bikes, no dogs, no fires, and almost twenty miles of connecting trails. With no bikes and no dogs, it tends to be the quieter walk. Facilities are minimal, so arrive self-sufficient.

Loch Lomond Recreation Area

Loch Lomond, the City of Santa Cruz's drinking water reservoir near Felton, has hiking trails with reservoir views, picnic areas, and boat rentals, but its rules are the strictest here because you're walking around a water supply. It's open seasonally, March through October, and closed every Wednesday. Through Labor Day the schedule is 7 a.m. to 8 p.m., Thursday through Tuesday; after Labor Day it drops to weekends only until the season ends the second weekend of October. Day use is $10 per vehicle. Swimming is prohibited, leashed dogs are welcome on trails, and staying on designated trails is part of the deal.

Walks without leaving town

You don't have to drive at all for a stroll. Garrahan Park, at 15555 Highway 9 just north of town, has a walking track, open sunrise to sunset. Junction Park and the rest of the in-town options are covered in our parks and playgrounds guide, and if your idea of a trail ends at the water, the river swimming guide covers that side of summer.

Mountain sense, briefly

A few habits keep local hikes uneventful. Poison oak grows along most trails here, so learn its three-leaf look and stay on the path. Carry more water than seems necessary; the ridge parks get hot and Big Basin has no potable water. Cell coverage dies in every park on this list, so download maps first and tell someone where you're going. And the standing rule: conditions change, so check the park's own page the morning you head out.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the closest hiking to downtown Boulder Creek?

Miller Property County Park on Kings Creek Road, about three miles north, is the closest dedicated trail area, and Garrahan Park's walking track is right on Highway 9. For a bigger day, Big Basin is nine miles up Highway 236.

Is Big Basin open for hiking?

Yes, for limited day use while it recovers from the 2020 fire, with camping still closed. What's open changes, so read our Big Basin status guide and confirm on the official park page before you drive up.

Can I bring my dog?

It depends on the park, so check before you load the car. Miller Property and Loch Lomond welcome leashed dogs on their trails, while Castle Rock and Henry Cowell's Fall Creek Unit don't allow dogs at all. Each park's own page has the current rule.

Do these parks charge entrance fees?

The state parks and Loch Lomond each list $10 per vehicle for day use; Big Basin runs $6 plus a $2 fee with a parking reservation, or $10 without. Miller Property and Garrahan Park list no day-use fee. Fees change; treat these as a snapshot.

When is Loch Lomond open?

March through October, and never on a Wednesday. Through Labor Day it's open Thursday to Tuesday, 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.; after that it's weekends only until the second weekend of October. Confirm on the city's Loch Lomond page before you go.

miller-property-boulder-creek.title: Miller Property County Park: Boulder Creek's Newest Place to Hike
miller-property-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek picked up a new park last year, and it's the kind that doesn't announce itself. Miller Property County Park sits on Kings Creek Road about three miles north of town, a short turn off Highway 9, and Santa Cruz County Parks opened it to the public in August 2025 after the land spent decades closed to nearly everyone. It's 410 acres along Kings Creek, open sunrise to sunset daily, and the quiet is the main amenity.

The opening delivered the basics, as the San Lorenzo Valley Post described it: a gated drive-through entry, a groomed dirt parking lot, a portable restroom, a picnic table, a temporary footbridge over the creek, and new signage on Highway 9. This is open space with a modest trail network, not a park with a lawn. Facilities are basic and still evolving, so arrive self-sufficient: water, a map that doesn't need a signal, and pack out what you pack in. Dogs are welcome on leash; fires, alcohol, and motorized vehicles aren't.

What's up there

The land climbs from the creek corridor through oak woodland, mixed evergreen forest, and grassland, and it holds about 38 acres of old-growth redwoods, per the Post's reporting. Kings Creek and Kings Creek Road split the property; the entrance sits about 1.2 miles off Highway 9. For now the walking follows a small network of informal trails near the creek, and no particular route is promised on a given day; parts of the property are an active work site.

The trail network that's coming

Santa Cruz Mountains Trail Stewardship and County Parks kicked off construction of a three-mile multi-use trail network in July 2026, with work running through spring 2027. The plan upgrades the existing informal trails and adds new connections, including a route to the old-growth grove, for hikers, cyclists, equestrians, and leashed dogs. If you'd rather build a trail than wait for one, SCMTS runs weekly public volunteer days at the property; the current schedule lives at santacruztrails.org/events. Separately, a shaded fuel break project with CAL FIRE will thin vegetation along Kings Creek Road to reduce wildfire risk, with early field days tentatively slated for December, per the Post.

How it became a park

The property carries eighty years of almost-was. As the Post tells it, Adolph C. Miller and Mary Sprague Miller deeded a portion of the land to the University of California in 1942, and UC Santa Cruz bought the rest in 1952. Part of it ran as a campground from 1967 to 1974. When the university declared the land surplus in the early 1990s, timber companies bid on it; the UC Regents turned them down and approved a $2.4 million sale to Save the Redwoods League in July 1994. The League donated the property to Santa Cruz County in March 2001, and then it sat, a park on paper, until Measure K, the half-cent sales tax county voters passed in March 2024, plus $100,000 in county funds, paid to open the gate. One holdover from the earlier eras made it through intact: the old pet cemetery is still up there.

Before you go

Check the county's Miller Property page for current conditions, especially while trail construction runs. Poison oak is a given along the creek, cell coverage is thin on Kings Creek Road, and there's no staffed anything at the property. For a groomed park instead, see our parks and playgrounds guide; for the big trail day, start with Big Basin's current status.

coffee-boulder-creek.title: Coffee in Boulder Creek: Where to Get a Cup
coffee-boulder-creek.html:
Boulder Creek has two coffee shops. Both are independent, both open before most of the town does, and both close by mid-afternoon, which tells you who they're built for: people starting a mountain day, not ending one. There's no Starbucks, no Peet's, and no drive-through anywhere in town, so a cup here means a local counter. That's the whole list, and this page sorts it by what kind of morning you're having.

Hours below are each business's posted hours as of this writing. Cafe schedules in this valley move with seasons and staffing, so call before you build a morning around one.

To sit a while: The Tree House Cafe

  • Address: 13266 Highway 9, at the north end of the business district
  • Phone: 831-610-8912
  • Posted hours: 6 a.m. weekdays, 7 a.m. weekends, closing 2:30 p.m. daily

The Tree House Cafe is the bigger of the town's two coffee rooms, an espresso bar with drip coffee, counter service, and living redwoods growing up through the floor and out the roof. The seating wraps around the trunks, which makes it the room locals settle into with a laptop, a notebook, or a long conversation. If your plan is a table and an hour, start here.

One thing to know before you look it up: the Tree House keeps no website. Its current hours and specials live on its Facebook and Instagram, and the phone gets answered. There's also an unrelated cafe with a near-identical name in Boulder Creek, Queensland, so if the page you found is in Australia, keep scrolling.

On your way out of town: Jenna Sue's Cafe

  • Address: 13090 Highway 9, mid-block downtown
  • Phone: 831-338-7008
  • Posted hours: 6 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. weekdays, 7 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. weekends

Jenna Sue's is the downtown coffeehouse and the commuter's stop: a small shop with a handful of seats, espresso drinks from americano through mocha plus drip, and food built for people who are on their way somewhere. The baking happens on site, so the case is stocked from the in-house bakery (Lori's coffee cake is named on the menu in its own right), along with pastries from Dessert First Bakery, which shares the kitchen.

My own order barely changes: the oatmeal loaded with fresh fruit, which I keep trying and failing to make at home. My partner is even more predictable; the astronaut breakfast wins every single time.

The beans are worth a line of their own. Jenna Sue's pours Java Bob's, a small-batch roaster based in Santa Cruz that has supplied cafes around the county for decades, and the cafe sells the beans by the bag as well as by the cup. Java Bob's doesn't keep a shop in Boulder Creek; Jenna Sue's counter is where you find it in town.

The 8 a.m. fallback: Johnnie's

Not every cup needs a cafe. Johnnie's Super Market at 13225 Highway 9 opens at 8 a.m. every day of the week and carries coffee in the store, with a bakery case a few steps away. It's the answer when both cafes have closed for the afternoon, since the market stays open until 9 most nights and 10 on Friday and Saturday. No espresso machine, but a hot cup and a pastry on a Sunday evening is a real option here and nowhere else in town.

If coffee is really breakfast

When the cup is just the opener, Bella's Cafe at 13132 Central Avenue is the sit-down diner: a plate, a table, and someone bringing eggs to you. It's not a coffee bar; it's breakfast as the main event. It serves 8 a.m. to 2 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday, and is closed Mondays. The full morning picture, including Scopazzi's weekend brunch, is in our breakfast guide, and everything beyond the morning is in where to eat in Boulder Creek.

Frequently Asked Questions

What opens earliest for coffee in Boulder Creek?

Jenna Sue's and the Tree House both post 6 a.m. openings on weekdays and 7 a.m. on weekends, the earliest doors in town. Those are posted hours as of this writing, so call ahead if you're planning a first-light start.

Is there a Starbucks or a drive-through in Boulder Creek?

No. Our directory doesn't list a national coffee chain or a drive-through anywhere in town. Coffee here comes from an independent counter or the grocery store, which is part of the character of the place.

Can I get coffee on a Monday?

Yes. Both cafes post Monday hours, which isn't true of most of the town's dining rooms, and Johnnie's is open daily from 8 a.m.

Whose coffee does Jenna Sue's pour?

Java Bob's Coffee Roasting, a Santa Cruz small-batch roaster. Jenna Sue's sells the beans by the bag as well as by the cup, so it's the place in town to pick some up for home.

notary-shipping-post-office-boulder-cree.title: Notary, Shipping, and the Post Office in Boulder Creek
notary-shipping-post-office-boulder-cree.html:
Paperwork errands stack up quietly: a package that has to go out, a signature that needs a notary, a passport renewal for a spring trip. In Boulder Creek some of that gets handled in town and some of it means a drive down the valley, and it isn't always obvious which is which. This guide sorts it errand by errand. The usual ground rule applies: inclusion isn't endorsement, and everything here comes from our verified business directory or the service's own published information, checked August 7, 2026.

The post office: 200 Lorenzo Street

  • Address: 200 Lorenzo Street, Boulder Creek
  • Phone: 831-338-4865
  • Retail counter: Monday through Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.; closed weekends
  • Lobby and PO boxes: Monday through Saturday, 6 a.m. to 5 p.m.; closed Sunday

The town's post office sits just off the main drag on Lorenzo Street, and for most mailing errands it's all you need: stamps, package drop-off, Priority Mail, hold mail, and PO boxes, which you can reserve online through usps.com. Box mail is up by 11 a.m., and the lobby opens at 6 a.m. Monday through Saturday, so early risers can check a box long before the counter opens.

Two timing details worth knowing. The retail counter closes on weekends, but on Saturday mornings from 6:30 to 11 a.m. you can still pick up a package the carrier left a notice for. And the last outgoing collection is 4:30 p.m. on weekdays and 1 p.m. on Saturday, so a Saturday afternoon drop won't move until Monday. Brookdale keeps its own small office too, at 105 Pacific Avenue, open weekdays 9 a.m. to noon and 1 to 3:30 p.m.

Getting a document notarized

Boulder Creek doesn't have a storefront notary office. What it has instead is arguably more convenient: mobile notaries who come to you. Two serve the valley with verified listings in our directory. Shandra Hunt Mobile Notary is based right in Boulder Creek and works evenings and weekends, handling general notary work plus loan signings, trusts, powers of attorney, and affidavits at California's standard rate of $15 per signature plus a travel fee; call 831-334-0748. Christina Wise Mobile Notary, based in Felton, covers the valley seven days a week from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. for loan signings and general notary work; call 831-588-0540.

The other route people try is the bank. Liberty Bank's Boulder Creek branch at 13233 Highway 9 is open weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., but its site doesn't publish notary details, so call 831-338-6477 and ask before you count on it.

Shipping with UPS or FedEx

USPS is the easy carrier in town; the post office is the only place in Boulder Creek to hand a package to a carrier. For UPS and FedEx you have two moves: schedule a home pickup, or drive to their locations.

The pickup is the mountain answer. Both UPS and FedEx let you schedule a pickup from your door through their websites, which turns a drive down the valley into a label and a doorstep handoff. For anything prelabeled, that's usually the least effort.

If you'd rather drop off in person, UPS means Scotts Valley: The UPS Store at 216 Mount Hermon Road for full service, or the UPS Access Point inside CVS at 257 Mount Hermon Road for prelabeled drop-offs. FedEx's own locator shows nothing in Boulder Creek and nothing in Felton either; the nearest options are FedEx at Walgreens, 210 Mount Hermon Road in Scotts Valley, PostalAnnex at 5610 Scotts Valley Drive, Suite B, which handles both FedEx and UPS under one roof, and a full FedEx store in Santa Cruz.

One more Scotts Valley trick: the post office at 241 Kings Village Road has a self-service kiosk in its lobby, open 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Saturday and 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sunday, the only Sunday shipping option anywhere near the valley.

Passports and passport photos

The Boulder Creek post office doesn't offer passport services, but you don't have to leave the valley either. The Ben Lomond post office at 250 Main Street takes passport appointments weekdays from 9 to 11:30 a.m., accepts walk-ins Monday, Wednesday, and Friday from 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., and shoots passport photos weekdays until 2 p.m. Book through usps.com or call 831-336-3528. Scotts Valley's post office, for what it's worth, doesn't list passport services at all.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the Boulder Creek post office hours?

The retail counter at 200 Lorenzo Street is open Monday through Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. The lobby and PO boxes are accessible 6 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Saturday, and Saturday package pickup runs 6:30 to 11 a.m.

Can I get a passport at the Boulder Creek post office?

No. The nearest passport services are at the Ben Lomond post office, 250 Main Street, with appointments weekdays 9 to 11:30 a.m. and passport photos on site.

Is there a UPS or FedEx drop-off in Boulder Creek?

No. For UPS and FedEx, schedule a home pickup through their websites, or use their locations in Scotts Valley on Mount Hermon Road and Scotts Valley Drive. FedEx lists no Boulder Creek or Felton location.

Where can I get something notarized in Boulder Creek?

Two mobile notaries serve the valley and come to you: Shandra Hunt (831-334-0748, based in Boulder Creek, evenings and weekends) and Christina Wise (831-588-0540, daily 9 a.m. to 7 p.m.). Liberty Bank's branch may help account holders; call 831-338-6477 to ask.
